churches.assessment: Aldersgate Church in Lubbock was founded in 1985 when a preacher began knocking on doors inviting people to a new church experience — the first service was held August 4, 1985 in the gymnasium of All Saints Episcopal School. The congregation voted 97% to disaffiliate from the UMC and has joined the Global Methodist Church. Lead Pastor Ryan Smallwood (married to Amy, two adult sons Blake and Jeb) leads with a conversational teaching style. Notable: Emily Fisher serves as Next Gen Pastor, meaning women do serve in pastoral roles at this particular local church — a YELLOW flag on the gender rubric for readers committed to strictly male-only pastoral offices. The lopsided disaffiliation vote signals strong institutional orthodox commitment, however. Named for John Wesley's famous May 1738 Aldersgate Street conversion experience.

(An earlier version of this assessment tied him to Southern Wesleyan University and drew a Wesleyan Holiness inference; his own bio does not say that, so the inference is withdrawn pending re-review.) The church's language — 'grounded on grace and truth,' 'cares deeply for our city and its flourishing' — reflects city-engagement theology which can trend progressive. This church is not an automatic green — the non-denominational structure warrants careful doctrinal investigation before committing. Visit but verify.

churches.assessment: All Saints Anglican is a standout conservative Anglican congregation in Ivy, just west of Charlottesville. Father Sean McDermott leads a parish rooted in the Anglican Province of America — a body that explicitly departed from the theologically liberal Episcopal Church (TEC) to maintain orthodox Christianity. The parish is notably associated with Ken Myers, founder of Mars Hill Audio Journal, as choir director — giving it an unusual depth of cultural and theological engagement. The APA ordains men only, holds to the 39 Articles, and maintains the historic Book of Common Prayer tradition. For a man drawn to liturgical worship, ancient prayer traditions, and sound orthodox theology, All Saints is exceptional. Note: APA is distinct from both TEC (liberal) and ACNA (the other Anglican break).

churches.assessment: All Saints Church in New Holland, PA (Lancaster County) was established in 1999 as a church plant of Christ Church (Moscow, ID) and is a member of the CREC. Dr. Gregg Strawbridge served faithfully as pastor for twenty years (2002–2022) and is the founder of the Strawbridge Ministerial Forum hosted by the church. Following his passing in 2022, Rev. Kasey Horvath (lead) and Rev. Brandon Gilanyi (associate) were installed in 2023, and the congregation relocated to a historic building in New Holland in 2024. Theologically this is a classic Moscow-network CREC congregation: Reformed, covenant-renewal liturgical worship, paedocommunion, classical Christian education ethos, patriarchal household vision, and postmillennial cultural engagement. The one area calling for direct inquiry is soteriology — CREC churches have historically been associated with Federal Vision theology, which modifies traditional Reformed articulations of justification. Ask the elders directly about their position on FV and justification. For a Reformed man in Lancaster County seeking a serious, liturgical, Moscow-aligned CREC home, this is the obvious first visit.

score_notes.christology: Orthodox Trinitarian per movement statement; deity of Christ affirmed.
score_notes.scripture: 'The Bible is the inspired, authoritative, living, eternally reliable Word of God without error in its original manuscript' — explicit inerrancy.
score_notes.gender: Antioch movement practices complementarian senior-pastor model with husband-wife team framing; policies on women elders vary by congregation. Waco pastor Jimmy Seibert (male).
score_notes.leadership: Founder/Senior Pastor Jimmy Seibert; movement headquartered at Waco. Apostolic-network model with strong founder personality.
score_notes.soteriology: Emphasis on 'repentance, faith, and a personal relationship with Jesus Christ' — evangelical framing; specific sola fide language not quoted.
score_notes.cultural: 'Traditional evangelical views on social issues, including a strong stance against abortion and homosexuality' — conservative.
score_notes.denominational: Six named male elders on public elder page — Jimmy Seibert, Vincent Carpenter, Mark Owen, Jeff Abshire, Carl Gulley, Jason Ramos — plus external advisors (Joe Ewen, Ron/Janine Parrish). Antioch International Movement of Churches (AIM) provides apostolic-network accountability with 45+ nations. Meets refined YELLOW: elder plurality + named network affiliation. Upgrade denominational from RED to YELLOW.
score_notes.preaching: Charismatic-evangelical preaching; not classically expository verse-by-verse.
score_notes.mission: 'Family of Spirit-led and biblically based churches that embrace every nation, tribe, people and language' — strong missions emphasis; 45+ nations.
score_notes.validation_2026_04: Homepage fetched 2026-04-23 — no Wayback snapshot. '5 Circles of Church' framework (personal devotion, life-on-life discipleship, house-to-house, gathered worship, witness) confirmed. Sunday 9/11 AM + Spanish 1:30 PM. Ministries: Kids, Youth, College, Young Adults, Spanish, Single Moms; worship/prayer/discipleship/prophetic streams. Alpha used for evangelism. No SOF, no elder roster, no Jimmy Seibert bio surfaced on homepage (pulled from prior enrichment). 'Prophetic' ministry stream is consistent with charismatic AIM tradition. No Comer/Kendi/DiAngelo, no affirming/egalitarian language. Existing yellow held — apostolic-network model with strong founder personality keeps caution; AIM elder plurality confirmed in prior enrichment.

score_notes.christology: Christ alone. Presuppositional apologetics places Christ as Lord over all knowledge and reasoning.
score_notes.scripture: Inerrancy affirmed without compromise. Scripture is the self-attesting Word of God — ultimate authority.
score_notes.gender: Patriarchal. Durbin holds firmly to male headship in home and church. No women in pastoral or elder roles.
score_notes.leadership: Homepage identity focuses on mission/ministries; specific elder board and Durbin's role not detailed on home landing — prior research retained.
score_notes.soteriology: Reformed soteriology (doctrines of grace). Justification by faith alone. Clear gospel preaching.
score_notes.cultural: Durbin is one of the most culturally engaged pastors in America — active in anti-abortion ministry outside clinics, fights LGBTQ ideology, opposes CRT. Unapologetically counter-cultural.
score_notes.preaching: Expository with strong apologetic application. Apologia Studios extends teaching reach globally via podcast and YouTube.
score_notes.mission: Homepage confirms End Abortion Now national campaign, Red Door Ministry abortion-clinic outreach, and Apologia Studios gospel-centered media — highly active evangelism and cultural engagement verified.
score_notes.mens_discipleship: Strong emphasis on men leading families. Church culture is distinctly masculine and confrontational (in the best sense).
score_notes.denominational: Reformed Baptist — confessional accountability with elder governance.

churches.assessment: Apologia Church under Jeff Durbin is one of the sharpest, most unapologetically Reformed and culturally engaged churches in America. Durbin combines expository preaching with presuppositional apologetics (Van Til/Bahnsen tradition), aggressive anti-abortion street ministry, and public debate against secularism and LGBTQ ideology. Apologia Studios is a major media platform. The church is small but punches far above its weight in cultural impact. GREEN across the board — this is exactly the kind of muscular, doctrine-driven, mission-active church MOOP celebrates.

churches.assessment: Apostles Anglican Church in west Knoxville is an ACNA parish in the Anglican Diocese of the South, led by Rector Rev. Jack King — who also serves as Dean of the Tennessee Convocation (ADOTS). He has been rector for over 13 years, providing mature pastoral leadership. The church is known for its 'scruffy hospitality' ethos and has been profiled in ACNA communications. The parish maintains one of the richest liturgical rhythms profiled here: Sunday services at 8:45 AM (with choral music), 11:15 AM (with acoustic music), plus 10:10 Formation Hour; Monday-Thursday daily Morning Prayer (8:30 AM), Midday Prayer (noon), and Evening Prayer (4:00 PM); and a Wednesday Noon Eucharist with Healing Service. Three strategic priorities include becoming a mother church, deepening spiritual formation across all ages, and serving the local neighborhood. ACNA 39 Articles framework with male-only ordination. Strong green-rated Anglican option for the Knoxville metro.

churches.overall_label: Strong Theological Alignment

score_notes.christology: ACNA congregation; Apostles' and Nicene Creeds affirmed as part of Anglican tradition.
score_notes.scripture: Bible-believing evangelical posture; inerrancy typically affirmed.
score_notes.gender: Male pastoral leadership observed; complementarian baseline (CBMW halfway position; MOOP holds patriarchal headship as the biblical standard).
score_notes.leadership: Male pastor(s) confirmed via church website.
score_notes.soteriology: Historic evangelical gospel of grace through faith alone.
score_notes.cultural: No DEI/CRT language surfaced on homepage; tagline 'Forming Whole Disciples of Jesus'.
score_notes.preaching: Sermons archive with weekly Bible-grounded preaching; Anglican lectionary-informed teaching.
score_notes.mission: Great Commission language via 'forming whole disciples'; Cedar Project and outreach ministries.
score_notes.mens_discipleship: Not explicitly listed as distinct men's ministry on homepage navigation — verify in person.
score_notes.denominational: ACNA — orthodox Anglican, broke from TEC for biblical fidelity.

churches.assessment: Apostles Uptown is part of the Apostles Church family in Manhattan, part of the ACNA (Anglican Church in North America) — the orthodox Anglican body that separated from TEC over biblical fidelity. Focused on "forming whole disciples of Jesus." ACNA affirms Scripture, historic creeds, and male ordination in most dioceses.
churches.enrichment_notes: ACNA baseline; no red flags on public site.

For men seeking a theologically clear conservative Baptist church, BGAV affiliation warrants caution and an in-person investigation to determine where this specific congregation lands doctrinally.

churches.assessment: Bel Air Church (formerly Bel Air Presbyterian Church) is the historic Presbyterian congregation on Mulholland Drive in Los Angeles, founded 1956. Ronald and Nancy Reagan joined as official members after leaving the White House in 1989 and worshiped there until their deaths. Donn D. Moomaw, the long-time former senior pastor, gave the invocation at President Reagan's first inauguration in 1981 and presided at his funeral. Bel Air did not depart to ECO during the 2012-2015 PCUSA exodus when over 100,000 conservative PCUSA members left for ECO: A Covenant Order of Evangelical Presbyterians — Bel Air stayed PCUSA, which institutionally has departed from biblical authority on sexual ethics and ordains women as elders and pastors at every level. Current senior pastor is Rev. Dr. Drew Sams. Per MOOP rubric this is RED at the denominational level; included for situational awareness about Ronald Reagan's home church.
churches.denomination_detail: PCUSA — stayed with the denomination through the 2012-2015 ECO departure wave; rebranded "Bel Air Church" but remains PCUSA.
churches.gender_detail: PCUSA permits women at all levels of ordination; egalitarian.

churches.assessment: Bethany Grace Fellowship in East Earl, Pennsylvania is one of the founding congregations of the Alliance of Mennonite Evangelical Congregations (AMEC) — the conservative Anabaptist-evangelical body that broke from the Mennonite Church USA merger in 2002 over doctrinal and sexuality concerns. Founded in 1957 as Blue Ball Mennonite Church, renamed Bethany Mennonite, and now Bethany Grace Fellowship, the congregation is led by Lead Pastor Steve Benedict. AMEC's two-fold confessional commitment — to evangelical orthodoxy and to historic biblical Anabaptism — gives this church the theological clarity that newer MC USA progressive drift lacks. For a Lancaster County man wanting a complementarian, biblically-grounded, Anabaptist-pietist congregation with explicit orthodoxy commitments and full ministry portfolio, Bethany Grace Fellowship is a strong candidate.

churches.assessment: Bethlehem Baptist Church is one of Virginia's most historically significant Baptist congregations, founded in 1838 in Northside Richmond. Church records trace roots to 1790 and include the legacy of Nannie Bland David, missionary to Africa (1880-1885) — the kind of Great Commission heritage that should be honored. Today the congregation is a BGAV member under Rev. George Brown's leadership. The standard BGAV concerns apply: no inerrancy requirement, women in ministry permitted, moderate denominational framework. Rev. Brown's theological convictions are unknown. Bethlehem's deep Baptist mission heritage makes it worth a visit — if the current congregation has maintained evangelical convictions within the BGAV framework, it could be a valuable kingdom partner for USMC Ministries. churches.assessment: Bloomington Chapel BIC traces its roots to 1928 when BIC preacher Albert Engle held a successful tent meeting near Columbia, Kentucky — the first BIC outreach in Adair County. The congregation outgrew its original schoolhouse meeting space, moved to a new building in 1960, called its first live-in pastor in 1989, and completed a new 250-275 seat facility in January 2013. Pastor Ralph Foster currently leads. The century-long continuous Anabaptist witness in this rural Kentucky community gives Bloomington Chapel real weight. Yellow rating per denominational caveat; local male leadership and historic accountability give substantial balance.

churches.assessment: Blue Ridge Grace Brethren Church has a remarkable 100-year history in Winchester, Virginia — founded in 1925 as the First Brethren Church of Winchester after a pioneering group of believers sold homemade cruellers to fund construction. This is the kind of sacrificial church-building story that marks a serious congregation. The Fellowship of Grace Brethren Churches provides accountability within a conservative evangelical, dispensationally informed tradition. Bible teaching is central to Grace Brethren DNA, with a doctrinal affirmation of Scripture's inerrancy and final authority. The Winchester Shenandoah Valley context gives this church a community role stretching back a century. For a man in Winchester or Frederick County wanting a smaller, doctrinally stable evangelical church with deep local roots, Blue Ridge Grace Brethren is worth visiting.

churches.assessment: The Bible Presbyterian Church on Grand Island, New York is part of the Bible Presbyterian Church's Great Lakes Presbytery. Senior Pastor Dr. Kevin M. Backus holds a Ph.D. — unusually strong academic credentials for a small-denomination pastor. The BPC was formed in 1937 by Carl McIntire, J. Oliver Buswell, and Allan MacRae as a conservative fundamentalist-leaning breakaway Presbyterian denomination holding the Westminster Standards with a pronounced emphasis on biblical inerrancy and separation from liberalism. The denomination is very small (only 28 churches across the US and one in Canada) — MOOP readers considering BPC congregations should understand they will likely find a small, tight-knit, strongly-convictional Reformed fellowship rather than a large-church experience. Green-rated orthodox Reformed option for the Buffalo, NY metro.

churches.assessment: Bridge Church Fredericksburg has one of the cleanest statements of faith among the churches surveyed: Trinitarian, Bible as final authority, salvation by grace through faith, baptism as response (not requirement), Great Commission-focused. The church was launched in 2019 by Max Lucado and the Oak Hills Church (San Antonio) team — Jimmy Pruitt was the former campus pastor who was invited by Max to take it independent. That's a vote of confidence from one of the most respected evangelical communicators of our generation. The two-service Sunday model with sermon notes and discipleship resources indicates a substantive ministry rather than a casual social gathering. Main watch items: no explicit complementarian statement, no formal denominational accountability, no confirmed men's ministry. The 'inter-denominational' description means Moop would need to probe the gender/leadership question directly before committing. Overall one of the more theologically promising independent churches in the FXBG area.

churches.address: 201 W Duke of Gloucester St, Williamsburg, VA 23185
churches.pastor_credentials: Interim Rector serving during clergy leadership transition; previously served in Dioceses of Kentucky, Southwestern Virginia, and South Carolina; Episcopal (TEC) ordained priest
churches.denomination: The Episcopal Church (TEC) — Diocese of Southern Virginia
churches.services: Multiple services including weekday worship; Sunday services (see website for current schedule)
churches.overall_label: TEC parish with female clergy; disqualifying on Biblical Design

score_notes.gender: TEC ordains women as priests and bishops. Bruton Parish currently has an interim rector (male) during transition, but the denomination officially allows and practices female ordination at all levels including bishops.
score_notes.cultural: TEC has been a leader among mainline denominations in embracing progressive cultural norms — LGBTQ affirmation, inclusive language for God, and departure from historic Anglican sexual ethics are TEC institutional positions.
score_notes.christology: TEC's theological diversity allows significant variation in congregational beliefs — from evangelical Anglicanism to universalism. Bruton Parish's own theology needs direct investigation, as TEC does not enforce doctrinal uniformity.
score_notes.soteriology: TEC does not hold a uniform soteriology. Without specific knowledge of Bruton Parish's preaching and doctrinal commitments, soteriology cannot be confirmed as orthodox.
score_notes.mens_discipleship: No dedicated men's ministry found. TEC context makes robust biblical men's discipleship formation less likely.
score_notes.denominational: The Episcopal Church (TEC) — Diocese of Southern Virginia is institutionally apostate — departed from biblical authority on sexuality, gender, and marriage.
score_notes.scripture: TEC tradition treats Scripture, tradition, and reason as co-equal authorities (Anglican triad / Hooker's three-legged stool); no inerrancy statement on site.
score_notes.leadership: Clergy page lists The Rev'd Lauren M. McDonald as Associate Rector for Outreach & Women's Ministries — female clergy in authoritative teaching/presiding role. Interim Rector The Rev'd William J. Watson III (male).
score_notes.preaching: 'Biblically-based liturgy, preaching and music' within Anglican tradition; Rite I/II Eucharistic framework. Mixed liturgical-expository rather than verse-by-verse.
score_notes.mission: Welcome statement: 'We welcome all into a Christ-centered community that nurtures and values each member.' Mission generic; no explicit gospel-proclamation framing.

churches.assessment: Bruton Parish Episcopal Church is one of America's most historically significant churches — established 1674, it hosted George Washington, Thomas Jefferson, Patrick Henry, and George Mason during the colonial era. The building is a National Historic Landmark in Colonial Williamsburg. However, historical significance does not equal current theological fidelity. Bruton Parish remains within The Episcopal Church (TEC) — a denomination that has departed from biblical sexual ethics, ordains women to all levels of ministry including bishop, officially endorses same-sex marriage, and has seen wholesale theological drift from orthodox Christianity. The congregation is currently in transition (interim rector). For a man committed to biblical inerrancy, male-only pastoral leadership, and historic Christian sexual ethics, Bruton Parish's TEC affiliation disqualifies it as a primary home church. Worth visiting as a historic site — not recommended as a spiritual home.
churches.gender_detail: Female Associate Rector (Rev Lauren M. McDonald) confirmed on clergy page — disqualifying per rubric (women in pastoral office).

churches.assessment: Bunker Hill BIC is a Brethren in Christ congregation in West Virginia's Eastern Panhandle, led by Pastor Kelly Day. The Brethren in Christ denomination is an unusual blend of Anabaptist, Pietist, and Wesleyan-Holiness streams, holding to believers' baptism by immersion, peace witness, and an emphasis on personal holiness. The local congregation appears stable with active Sunday services. The denominational caveat is real: BIC U.S. has ordained women since the 1980s, so men seeking a tightly complementarian polity should ask about local elder/teaching practice before committing. The Anabaptist DNA does provide doctrinal accountability and a peace-church witness that some find compelling.

churches.assessment: Burke Community Church under Dr. Marty Baker is a nondenominational evangelical church with impressive pastoral credentials. A Dallas Theological Seminary Th.M. in Old Testament and a Southern Evangelical Seminary D.Min. in Apologetics — that's serious academic formation in a conservative evangelical tradition. Baker has served over 30 years, which means this is not a personality-driven flash-in-the-pan; it's a stable, long-tenured pastoral ministry. BCC is known for its 'family feel' in a church that serves a community area effectively. Two Sunday services, men's and women's ministry infrastructure, and hosting a regional missions conference all signal a healthy, outward-focused congregation. For a man in Burke, Fairfax County, or Springfield, BCC is a strong nondenominational option.

churches.assessment: Butter Valley Community Church in Bally, Pennsylvania — formerly known as Hereford Mennonite Church — was the leading congregation that organized the Alliance of Mennonite Evangelical Congregations (AMEC) in 2001-2002 when conservative Anabaptists departed Mennonite Church USA over doctrinal and sexuality concerns. Robert Gerhart, then-pastor, was the primary AMEC organizer. Today Pastor Mark Hager leads with Caleb McCarthy as Associate Pastor. AMEC's two-fold confessional commitment to evangelical orthodoxy and historic biblical Anabaptism gives this congregation rare theological clarity for a Mennonite-rooted body. For a Berks County or Boyertown-area man wanting a complementarian, biblically-grounded, Anabaptist-pietist congregation with explicit orthodoxy heritage, Butter Valley is one of the strongest options in southeastern Pennsylvania.

churches.assessment: Calvary Chapel Fredericksburg checks most of the boxes Moop cares about. The Calvary Chapel movement is known above all for verse-by-verse expository Bible teaching — it's baked into the DNA (Chuck Smith legacy). The leadership page shows a clear elder/pastor structure with male pastoral leadership, a dedicated Men's Ministry leader (Joe Gallegos), and a full complement of ministries including youth, children, prayer, and outreach. CC churches typically hold to Scripture inerrancy, salvation by grace through faith alone, and complementarian leadership. The charismatic-adjacent culture (CC is Spirit-friendly but not charismatic in the more extreme sense) may be a moderate fit for Moop's background. The verse-by-verse preaching model is one of the best in evangelical Christianity. Strong candidate.

churches.assessment: Calvary Fellowship Mennonite Church was established in 1968 in Blackville, South Carolina, when a group of Mennonite families from Ohio and Indiana relocated to the area. Affiliated with the Beachy Amish-Mennonite Fellowship, the church practices plain Anabaptist witness with bishop/minister/deacon polity, male-only ordination, plain dress, women's head covering, and a simple agricultural lifestyle. The congregation also operates Calvary Fellowship Mennonite School. Pastor Sam Troyer leads per 2023-2024 records. The Beachy tradition arose from a 1927 division in the Casselman River Old Order Amish in Pennsylvania, led by Bishop Moses M. Beachy — adopting evangelical outreach while maintaining plain Anabaptist conviction. Green rating.

score_notes.christology: LCMS subscribes unconditionally to the Book of Concord (1580) — Nicene/Athanasian/Apostles Creeds confessed each Lord's Day. Trinitarian orthodox.
score_notes.scripture: LCMS holds verbal-plenary inspiration and inerrancy of Scripture (Brief Statement 1932, A Statement of Scriptural Principles).
score_notes.gender: LCMS ordains only qualified men to the pastoral office; complementarian by confession (1969 New Orleans convention; reaffirmed 2004).
score_notes.leadership: Male-only pastors; lay board of elders + congregational governance per LCMS polity. Head Elder Jacob Geigle; Chairman Shane Jaco.
score_notes.soteriology: Sola fide / sola gratia / sola scriptura per Book of Concord; Augsburg Confession Article IV (Justification by Faith).
score_notes.cultural: LCMS denominationally resists DEI/CRT framing; conservative confessional posture. Local congregation alignment presumed consistent with LCMS.
score_notes.preaching: LCMS preaching follows lectionary + Law/Gospel distinction; typically expository within liturgical frame.
score_notes.mission: Standard LCMS missions cooperation; specific local mission emphasis not documented on homepage fetch.
score_notes.mens_discipleship: No dedicated men's ministry visible on church staff page or homepage. Lutheran Women's Missionary League (LWML) coordinator listed but no parallel men's body identified.
score_notes.denominational: LCMS Southeastern District — strong confessional accountability via Synod, Circuit Visitor, and district President.

churches.assessment: Calvary Lutheran Church in Jacksonville, NC is part of the Lutheran Church—Missouri Synod — one of the most confessionally faithful Lutheran bodies in the U.S. LCMS holds inerrancy of Scripture, justification by faith alone, the bodily resurrection, male-only pastoral ordination, and a Trinitarian creedal Christology rooted in the Book of Concord. The church's "Divine Service" liturgical format (8:00 AM and 10:30 AM Sundays, with Adult Bible Study and Sunday School at 9:15 AM) is the historic Lutheran Mass — Law and Gospel preaching, Word and Sacrament. Located at 206 Pine Valley Rd and serving Marines and families from Camp Lejeune and MCAS New River, this church offers a stable, confessional alternative in a region dominated by Baptist and Methodist congregations. The pastor name is not displayed on the staff page (a link to "Meet Our Pastor" exists but content was not directly verifiable on fetch), so verify pastor on visit. Men's ministry is not visibly advertised — Lutheran congregations often run men's formation through Bible classes and Lutheran Hour Ministries rather than branded "men's ministry" — but worth asking on a visit. Strong recommendation for confessional Lutheran or liturgically-minded Christians in the Onslow County area.

churches.assessment: The Cathedral of St. Matthew the Apostle is DC's most historically significant Catholic church — site of President Kennedy's funeral Mass in 1963 and the Red Mass for the US Supreme Court each October. For USMC Ministries, it is important to understand this institution in the DC context, especially for Catholic veterans and their families. From a Protestant evangelical standpoint, the core soteriology concern is real: Roman Catholicism does not affirm justification by faith alone in Christ alone. For Catholic-background veterans, this is a place of genuine spiritual heritage. For Protestant-background men seeking Gospel clarity, the soteriology differences require honest acknowledgment. Included here for denominational context and situational awareness — DC military/government personnel will have Catholic colleagues and this cathedral represents their tradition with dignity.

YELLOW — impressive scale but needs verification on gender theology, expository commitment, and cultural backbone.

churches.assessment: Chancellor Baptist's doctrinal statement is genuinely solid — they affirm Scripture as God's Word, salvation through Christ alone, eternal security, baptism by immersion, Great Commission evangelism. The church's mission statement (pointing people to Christ and into His church) is clear and healthy. The honest concern is BGAV affiliation: unlike SBC, BGAV is the moderate Virginia Baptist stream that parted ways over inerrancy and women's ordination. That doesn't automatically mean Chancellor is progressive — many BGAV churches are theologically conservative at the local level — but the accountability structure is to a moderate denomination. Before joining, Moop should ask: Does Chancellor have an elder board? What is the stance on women in pastoral roles? Pastor Cameron West's background and convictions are unknown — worth a direct conversation.

churches.assessment: Oldest Episcopal church in Kentucky (founded 1796 by Rev. James Moore, first rector and first president of Transylvania University). Present Gothic structure built 1848 by John McMurtry. Henry Clay was a founding pewholder when the parish was organized August 25, 1808; he funded a family pew though he did not formally join until 1847 at age 70 (baptized by Rev. Berkley at Ashland on June 22, 1847 because the church was under construction; confirmed by Bishop Benjamin Bosworth Smith at Transylvania's Morrison Hall on July 18, 1847). Now the cathedral of the Episcopal Diocese of Lexington under Dean Carol Wade. RED per TEC rubric.

For a man wanting serious Reformed theology and strong masculine leadership culture in DC, Christ Kirk is worth serious consideration.

churches.assessment: Christ Methodist Church of Auburn is a post-2022 Global Methodist plant, having voted to join the GMC and called Dr. Tony McCullough as their first senior minister in 2023. Nearly 700 members stood together at their first membership vows ceremony. The congregation currently gathers at the Greystone Office and Ministry Center while actively exploring permanent building options. As a GMC church, they affirm orthodox Wesleyan theology, traditional marriage, and the historic Christian faith — the specific reasons the GMC separated from the progressive UMC. Male lead pastor, active men's Bible study, and children's ministry make this a strong Methodist option for the Auburn area. The one caution flag is that the GMC's Alabama-Florida-West Georgia Conference ordination stance on women as elders should be verified; GMC varies by conference. Overall a green-eligible, solidly orthodox Wesleyan church worth further on-the-ground review.

churches.assessment: The Church at Clarendon has a female senior pastor — Pastor Danielle Bridgeforth — which places it outside the bounds of biblical complementarianism (1 Tim 2:12; 3:1-7). The American Baptist Churches USA (ABC) denomination is theologically moderate-to-liberal and affirms women's ordination, contrasting sharply with the SBC's Baptist Faith & Message 2000. The church may have sincere believers and Christ-centered sermons, but the pastoral leadership structure contradicts clear New Testament instruction on male-only elder/pastor roles. For a man serious about building his spiritual life in a doctrinally sound environment, The Church at Clarendon is not recommended as a primary home church.

The church's mission: 'Finding and Forming Disciples of Jesus Christ.' Church plants within the PCA carry the full weight of Reformed accountability — James River Presbytery oversight, Westminster Confession adherence, male-only elders, inerrancy of Scripture. The Church Hill neighborhood is exactly where Gospel-minded church planting belongs: a community with deep spiritual history and current spiritual need. For men with a heart for urban mission and Reformed doctrine, this is worth visiting.

churches.assessment: Church of the Incarnation is an ACNA church plant serving western Henrico County, meeting at Gayton Road Christian Church on Sundays at 9am. The Anglican Church in North America (ACNA) formed in 2009 when conservative Anglicans broke from the progressive Episcopal Church (TEC) over Scripture authority, sexuality, and leadership. ACNA holds to the 39 Articles, male clergy, traditional Anglican liturgy, and biblical sexual ethics — a clean break from TEC's progressive drift. The church's stated core values are compelling: 'Biblical teaching for the head and the heart; Spiritual formation through liturgy and sacrament; A life of prayer together; Gospel care for those in need; Discipleship of the next generation.' This is Word-and-sacrament Anglicanism done right. Strong option for men who love liturgical worship rooted in Scripture.

churches.assessment: Church of the Advent is one of Washington DC's most interesting evangelical Anglican church plants. Founded in 2007 by Tommy Hinson from a prayer meeting in Columbia Heights, Advent belongs to the ACNA — the orthodox Anglican body that separated from the theologically liberal Episcopal Church (TEC). The church explicitly describes its mission as 'seeking the flourishing of Washington, DC,' combining robust liturgical worship with urban community engagement. The ACNA framework provides the theological guardrails: Jerusalem Declaration, 39 Articles, male-only ordination, and confessional accountability. For any man in DC seeking Anglican worship without the progressive drift of TEC, Church of the Advent is a premier choice.

churches.assessment: Churchome — formerly The City Church, founded by Wendell Smith in 1992 — is now led by Wendell's son Judah Smith and Judah's wife Chelsea Smith as co-lead pastors. Chelsea holds the same top pastoral title as Judah and preaches Sunday services. Church Clarity scores Churchome "Clear: Egalitarian" on women in leadership. Per MOOP rubric (female pastor at senior level → RED), this is a hard RED on gender and leadership. Additional concerns: (1) LGBTQ policy is publicly Undisclosed — Chelsea Smith answered the gay-pastor question with rhetorical inclusion rather than a policy answer; (2) T.D. Jakes — historically associated with Oneness/modalist Christology — joined the Churchome board around 2021, raising Trinity-adjacency concerns even though Churchome itself is formally Trinitarian; (3) the celebrity-pastor culture (Justin Bieber and other A-list members) and Churchome app-driven model represent a particular branch of attractional evangelicalism that prioritizes accessibility over doctrinal precision. The Belltown Seattle campus at 2700 1st Ave is the flagship location. Judah Smith is a gifted communicator; the preaching is grace-focused, narrative, and culturally engaged. But the egalitarian leadership structure, LGBTQ ambiguity, and board composition make this RED per MOOP convictions. This is NOT Mars Hill (which dissolved 2014 under Mark Driscoll); Churchome is a different church with a different doctrinal posture. Adam visited Churchome in Seattle.

churches.assessment: Columbia Baptist Church (now branding as 'Columbia Church') is a historic Baptist congregation founded in 1856 by abolitionists in Falls Church, VA. Led by co-pastors Dr. Jim Baucom and Dr. Kris Clifford (both male), the church is SBC-affiliated and emphasizes multicultural ministry with five language congregations. Concerns include: no explicit inerrancy statement visible, 'biblical justice' language that needs verification against CRT/DEI frameworks, a sermon series title suggesting therapeutic/topical preaching, no men's ministry, and a co-pastor model unusual for Baptist polity. The church's rebranding to 'Columbia Church' (dropping 'Baptist') may signal a move away from denominational identity. BGAV affiliation places it in the moderate Baptist tradition. Needs deeper evaluation of doctrinal positions and preaching content.

churches.address: 1501 Washington Ave, Fredericksburg, VA 22401 (former First Christian Church building; moved in February 2025); Office: 1715 Princess Anne St
churches.pastor: Gregg Jennings (Lead Pastor); Melissa Southall (Worship & Outreach Pastor, ordained 2021)
churches.pastor_credentials: Gregg Jennings: BA Ozark Christian College; MA Religion + MA Global Missions, Gordon-Conwell Theological Seminary; Lead Pastor since 2009
churches.founded: ~2004 (21 years as a mobile church; 12 years at The Old Silk Mill, 1707 Princess Anne St; moved to Washington Ave permanent home Feb 2025)
churches.services: Sundays 10:00 AM at 1501 Washington Ave; Easter: 6:30 AM river service + 9:00 AM & 11:00 AM Sanctuary services
churches.overall_label: WARNING! — Red in Priority Area

score_notes.christology: Gordon-Conwell trained lead pastor; Ozark Christian College background. Christ-centered mission language throughout. No pluralism indicators.
score_notes.scripture: Gordon-Conwell is a conservative evangelical seminary (D.A. Carson's home school), which suggests solid Scripture foundations. However, no inerrancy statement found; independent church context means local stance needs confirmation.
score_notes.gender: Melissa Southall serves as Worship & Outreach Pastor and was ordained in 2021. Female ordained staff in a named pastoral role indicates egalitarian practice regardless of lead pastor being male. Red — women serving in ordained pastoral authority.
score_notes.leadership: Church elders are mentioned on the leadership page (not enumerated publicly). Gregg Jennings is lead pastor. Independent; no formal denominational accountability outside local elder board.
score_notes.soteriology: Gordon-Conwell training and evangelical church DNA imply faith-alone. No explicit statement found publicly.
score_notes.cultural: Tagline 'make as much room at the table of Christ as possible' could signal inclusive-table theology or just genuine hospitality. Self-describes as 'a bit messy' (from new home announcement). No DEI/CRT language found, but the inclusive framing bears watching.
score_notes.preaching: No sermon library readily available to evaluate preaching style. 21-year track record suggests substance over novelty.
score_notes.mission: Gregg holds an MA in Global Missions from Gordon-Conwell; Great Commission language is present: 'glorify God, emulate Christ and serve our beautiful city.'
score_notes.mens_discipleship: Explicit 'Pour In Spirit: Men's Night' events on calendar — active men's programming.
score_notes.denominational: Fully independent. No denominational accountability beyond internal elders.

churches.assessment: Common Ground Church has a compelling origin story: 21 years as a mobile congregation finally receiving a permanent home — the historic First Christian Church building on Washington Ave, gifted free of charge by a 100-year-old congregation choosing to bless its successor. That kind of kingdom generosity, and CG's decision to then give their former meeting house (The Old Silk Mill space) to a Filipino congregation, shows genuine missional health. Lead Pastor Gregg Jennings trained at Gordon-Conwell Theological Seminary (among the most rigorous conservative evangelical seminaries), studied both Theology and Global Missions, and has pastored CG since 2009. The church has elders, active ministries including a men's night, kids, and youth programs. Main yellow flags: Melissa Southall holds a staff pastoral title and was ordained in 2021 (female ordained pastor in a worship/outreach role); the inclusive table language may reflect a broad-welcome posture or a softer ecclesiology — worth hearing a sermon and asking Gregg directly about his complementarian convictions and Scripture inerrancy. Overall a promising, established community church worth visiting.

score_notes.christology: OPC subscribes to the Westminster Standards — orthodox Trinitarian Christology, Chalcedonian two-natures, virgin birth, bodily resurrection.
score_notes.scripture: Westminster Confession ch. 1 affirms plenary verbal inspiration and inerrancy of the Scriptures as the only rule of faith and life.
score_notes.gender: OPC Book of Church Order restricts the offices of teaching elder, ruling elder, and deacon to qualified men only (1 Tim 2–3; Titus 1).
score_notes.leadership: Plurality of ordained male elders (session) under presbyterian polity with accountability to the presbytery and General Assembly.
score_notes.soteriology: Reformed soteriology per Westminster — monergistic regeneration, sola fide, sola gratia, sola Scriptura, effectual calling, perseverance of the saints.
score_notes.cultural: OPC historically resists theological accommodation to cultural pressure — Machen's legacy of confessional fidelity over cultural relevance.
score_notes.denominational: Orthodox Presbyterian Church — founded 1936 by J. Gresham Machen as a confessionally Reformed denomination against Modernism in the PCUSA.
score_notes.preaching: OPC pulpits are characterized by expository, Christ-centered, Law/Gospel preaching from the Westminster tradition.
score_notes.mens_discipleship: OPC congregations typically emphasize family worship, catechism instruction, and male headship in home and church — strong formation pipeline for men.
score_notes.mission: OPC Committee on Foreign Missions and Home Missions actively plants confessionally Reformed churches domestically and abroad.

churches.assessment: Community Presbyterian Church (OPC) is a congregation of the Orthodox Presbyterian Church (OPC), the confessional Reformed denomination founded in 1936 by J. Gresham Machen. OPC churches subscribe to the Westminster Confession of Faith and Catechisms, restrict ordained office to qualified men, and practice presbyterian polity with accountability through session, presbytery, and General Assembly. Baseline green rating reflects confessional identity; verify local particulars on the website.

score_notes.scripture: NBC-USA generally evangelical-Baptist on Scripture but lacks tight inerrancy confession; local posture varies.
score_notes.gender: NBC-USA varies congregation by congregation; Aker is male senior pastor but NBC-USA broadly permits women pastors.
score_notes.leadership: Male senior pastor; deacons + ministry-leader structure typical of NBC-USA.
score_notes.cultural: NBC-USA churches commonly engage social-justice themes; specific posture at Cornerstone not surveyed.
score_notes.preaching: Black-Baptist homiletic tradition — narrative-driven, not strict expository.
score_notes.mission: Bed-Stuy community engagement; Jeffries himself served as a Cornerstone usher in his youth, suggesting strong intergenerational discipleship.
score_notes.mens_discipleship: Cornerstone's usher culture (Jeffries became "white-gloved, dues-paying usher") indicates institutional formation of young men in service roles.
score_notes.denominational: NBC-USA — largest Black Baptist body; generally conservative on Christology and Scripture but progressive on race/justice; sexuality posture varies.

churches.assessment: Cornerstone Baptist Church at 574 Madison Street in Bedford-Stuyvesant, Brooklyn, is the lifelong home church of House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries (D-NY-8). Jeffries grew up in Crown Heights and was formed at Cornerstone — in his youth becoming one of the church's white-gloved, dues-paying ushers, tending to crying babies and handling neighborhood traffic during worship. Cornerstone is institutionally part of the National Baptist Convention USA, the largest historically Black Baptist denomination. Rev. Lawrence E. Aker III is current senior pastor. NBC-USA is generally evangelical-Baptist on core doctrine but specific posture on sexuality, women in pastoral ministry, and biblical inerrancy varies by congregation. Per MOOP rubric this is YELLOW — would need on-site verification of confessional posture and pulpit theology before a recommendation; included with notable-attendees context for the most prominent Democratic House leader.
churches.denomination_detail: National Baptist Convention USA — historic Black Baptist congregation in Bed-Stuy.
churches.gender_detail: Male senior pastor (Rev. Lawrence E. Aker III); NBC-USA denominational posture on women clergy varies congregation by congregation.

Live-fetched https://cbcbrooklyn.org/our-pastor/ + Brooklyn Eagle + Religion News Service + Word&Way + The Hill on 2026-05-16 — confirmed Rev. Lawrence E. Aker III as senior pastor + 574 Madison St Brooklyn NY 11221 + NBC-USA affiliation + Hakeem Jeffries lifelong member and former usher.

churches.assessment: Cornerstone Chapel is an Apostolic/Oneness Pentecostal church — and that's a hard stop for theological alignment. Oneness Pentecostalism denies the eternal distinction of the three persons of the Trinity (Father, Son, Holy Spirit), teaching instead that 'Jesus' is the only name of God and the three are merely different modes. This places it outside the bounds of Nicene orthodoxy — the same line historic Christianity drew in 325 AD. Additionally, most Apostolic churches teach that speaking in tongues and baptism in 'Jesus' name only' are necessary for salvation, adding works to justification. The congregation may be sincere and passionate, but the core theological framework disqualifies it for anyone committed to trinitarian Christianity and faith-alone soteriology. Not recommended.

churches.assessment: Cornerstone Chapel under Gary Hamrick is one of the strongest Bible-teaching churches in Northern Virginia. Founded in 1991 with 18 charter members, Hamrick has grown it into a thriving congregation through verse-by-verse exposition through every book of the Bible — the Calvary Chapel way. His Wednesday night teaching is particularly notable: a mid-week deep dive that many men would find more satisfying than a typical Sunday service. 30+ years of consistent, doctrinally sound, culturally clear pastoral leadership is rare and valuable. The Calvary Chapel association maintains complementarian polity and a high view of Scripture. For a man in Loudoun County or the western NoVA corridor, Cornerstone Chapel is a top-tier option. Note: task brief mentioned 'Skip Heitzig' — that is Pastor Skip Heitzig of Calvary Church in Albuquerque, NM. Gary Hamrick is Cornerstone Chapel's pastor.

Not recommended for men seeking expository, elder-led, Reformed or Baptist Christianity. May appeal to those in the charismatic/prophetic stream.

churches.name: Cornerstone Presbyterian Church (OPC)
churches.denomination_detail: Orthodox Presbyterian Church — Presbytery of Philadelphia
churches.overall_label: Confessionally Reformed — Strong

score_notes.christology: OPC subscribes to the Westminster Standards — orthodox Trinitarian Christology, Chalcedonian two-natures, virgin birth, bodily resurrection.
score_notes.scripture: Westminster Confession ch. 1 affirms plenary verbal inspiration and inerrancy of the Scriptures as the only rule of faith and life.
score_notes.gender: OPC Book of Church Order restricts the offices of teaching elder, ruling elder, and deacon to qualified men only (1 Tim 2–3; Titus 1).
score_notes.leadership: Plurality of ordained male elders (session) under presbyterian polity with accountability to the presbytery and General Assembly.
score_notes.soteriology: Reformed soteriology per Westminster — monergistic regeneration, sola fide, sola gratia, sola Scriptura, effectual calling, perseverance of the saints.
score_notes.cultural: OPC historically resists theological accommodation to cultural pressure — Machen's legacy of confessional fidelity over cultural relevance.
score_notes.denominational: Orthodox Presbyterian Church — founded 1936 by J. Gresham Machen as a confessionally Reformed denomination against Modernism in the PCUSA.
score_notes.preaching: OPC pulpits are characterized by expository, Christ-centered, Law/Gospel preaching from the Westminster tradition.
score_notes.mens_discipleship: OPC congregations typically emphasize family worship, catechism instruction, and male headship in home and church — strong formation pipeline for men.
score_notes.mission: OPC Committee on Foreign Missions and Home Missions actively plants confessionally Reformed churches domestically and abroad.

churches.assessment: Cornerstone Presbyterian Church (OPC) is a congregation of the Orthodox Presbyterian Church (OPC), the confessional Reformed denomination founded in 1936 by J. Gresham Machen. OPC churches subscribe to the Westminster Confession of Faith and Catechisms, restrict ordained office to qualified men, and practice presbyterian polity with accountability through session, presbytery, and General Assembly. Baseline green rating reflects confessional identity; verify local particulars on the website.

churches.assessment: Covenant Bible Church is a Reformed Baptist congregation in North Georgetown (Austin metro area) planted and led by pastor-theologian Joel Webbon. The church affirms the 1689 Second London Baptist Confession — one of the most rigorous and historically grounded confessions in Protestant Christianity — placing it firmly within the Reformed, biblical-patriarchy, and expository preaching tradition. Webbon is a nationally known voice through Right Response Ministries, openly advocating biblical patriarchy (he explicitly rejects the 'complementarian' label) and Christian Nationalism. He has headlined panels on biblical patriarchy alongside Doug Wilson, Eric Conn, and Dale Partridge, and the church is networked with Church & Family Life (Scott Brown). He has generated controversy for some of his political/cultural commentary — men should evaluate this directly rather than through secondhand coverage. The church's theological foundation is solid: Trinitarian, faith-alone soteriology, male eldership, expository preaching, and Great Commission focus. The one caution is independence — no formal denominational structure means accountability rests on the internal elder structure. For men in the Georgetown/Austin area seeking a doctrinally serious, unapologetically patriarchal church, this is worth a visit. Personal note: Connected to Joel Webb (Webbon) referenced in USMC Ministries network.

churches.assessment: Covenant Life Church has an extraordinary and complicated history. Founded in 1977 by C.J. Mahaney as a charismatic fellowship, it evolved into one of America's most theologically sophisticated Reformed evangelical churches — hosting conferences, producing discipleship resources, and nurturing a generation of serious Bible-saturated Christians. But CLC also became ground zero for significant controversies: the Sovereign Grace Churches abuse lawsuit (2012), C.J. Mahaney's leadership scandals, and most publicly — Joshua Harris (pastor 2004-2015) publicly deconstructing his faith in 2019 and renouncing Christianity. Current pastor Mark Mitchell leads a congregation that has weathered enormous institutional trauma. The theological framework (Reformed, complementarian, Gospel-centered) remains intact on paper. The questions are about institutional health, pastoral culture, and whether the congregation has genuinely processed and healed from years of controversy. Worth visiting with eyes wide open.

churches.enrichment_notes: Pastor succession update: Kevin Rogers now Lead Pastor (prior enrichment had Mark Mitchell). All pastoral staff male — reinforces complementarian green. Denominational affiliation (SGC vs. independent) still not explicitly stated on site.

The GMC Alabama-West Florida Conference stance on women elders should still be verified. Overall a strong green-eligible Wesleyan option in southeast Alabama.

churches.assessment: Covenant Presbyterian Church Harrisonburg is a PCA congregation under the Blue Ridge Presbytery — arguably the gold standard for Reformed evangelical accountability in American denominational life. The Westminster Confession of Faith provides the most rigorous doctrinal framework of any evangelical denomination. Rev. Todd Pruitt is a known Reformed voice who brings theological seriousness to pastoral ministry. Two full morning services (8:30 AM and 11:15 AM) signal a congregation of meaningful size with the infrastructure to support solid men's, children's, and discipleship ministries. The James Madison University context (Harrisonburg is a college town) gives Covenant opportunities for campus ministry and young adult outreach alongside its established membership. For a man in Harrisonburg or the Shenandoah Valley wanting the strongest Reformed confessional accountability available, Covenant Presbyterian is the benchmark.

churches.assessment: District Church is a multicultural, non-denominational congregation in Washington, DC founded by Aaron Graham in 2010. Graham holds a doctorate from Fuller Seminary and a public policy degree from Harvard. The church affirms Trinitarian theology and appears Christ-centered. However, several yellow flags: no explicit inerrancy statement, no visible elder/accountability structure, no men's ministry, and non-denominational independence means no external doctrinal guardrails. The church's heavy involvement in social causes (foster care, affordable housing) is commendable but requires verification that the gospel remains central rather than being displaced by social advocacy. No female pastors identified, but no explicit complementarian position either. Needs in-person evaluation to assess preaching depth and doctrinal rigor.

churches.assessment: Due West ARP Church sits in the historic home of Erskine College and Erskine Theological Seminary — the ARP-affiliated educational institutions that have nurtured the denomination's Southern Presbyterian identity since 1839. Pastor Rev. Scott Moore accepted the call in January 2021 after 15 years of missions ministry with World Witness in Mexico, where he taught at the Eben-Ezer Theological Seminary of the Mexican ARP. His academic credentials are exceptional: B.S. from Columbia International University, M.Div. from Reformed Theological Seminary Jackson, and Th.M. in New Testament from Westminster Theological Seminary Philadelphia (2017). He was ordained by Catawba Presbytery in 1995. The combination of rigorous Reformed theological training, Pauline New Testament specialization, and long-term missions experience makes this a strongly-credentialed pastor for a small-town ARP congregation. Green-rated orthodox Reformed option for the upstate South Carolina area.

churches.assessment: East Fairview Mennonite Church traces its roots to the 1870s migration of Amish Mennonite families from Ohio and Illinois to Nebraska. Formally organized in spring 1876 with 23 members and first pastor P. P. Hershberger, the congregation has continuously served the Milford area for 150 years and now reports 173 members. Pastor Kyle Roth currently leads. The deep generational continuity, strong CMC/Rosedale conservative Anabaptist accountability, and significant membership size make East Fairview a flagship Nebraska Mennonite congregation. Green rating reflects strong confessional, gender, and leadership integrity.

score_notes.preaching: Programmed worship with prepared sermons (not silent unprogrammed worship).
score_notes.mission: Friends Southwest church-planting + global missions tradition (e.g., Bolivia, Peru, Kenya through EFM).

churches.assessment: East Whittier Friends Church is the lifelong home meeting of Richard Milhous Nixon — the 37th President was raised here from age 9, played piano in Sunday school, taught Sunday school as a young attorney, and remained a member until his death in 1994. The congregation is part of Friends Southwest, the evangelical/programmed branch of Quakerism — distinct from the liberal unprogrammed Friends General Conference (FGC) and Friends United Meeting (FUM) which have moved toward LGBT affirmation. Evangelical Friends affirm Trinitarian orthodoxy, biblical authority, and grace-through-faith soteriology in the Richmond Declaration tradition. Worship is bilingual (English/Spanish) and programmed — looking more like a contemporary evangelical service than the silent meetings stereotypically associated with Quakers. Female pastoral leadership is present (Pastora Delia Madrid) — consistent with Quakerism's 17th-century affirmation of women in ministry, but yellow on MOOP's rubric. Solid green at the denominational and theological core; historic Americana.

Friends Journal + QuakerSpeak document Nixon's lifelong membership from age 9 until death 1994; he taught Sunday school and played piano. Pastor Eugene Coffin (deceased) was Nixon's pastor here and conducted White House services during Nixon presidency.

churches.name: Eastside Baptist Church
churches.address: 204 Eastland Drive North, Twin Falls, ID 83301
churches.pastor_credentials: Plurality of elders; 1689 confessional Reformed Baptist governance
churches.services: Sunday School 9:15 AM & 12:30 PM | Sunday Morning Worship 10:30 AM | Sunday Evening 5:30 PM | Wednesday 6:30 PM (Psalm reading, prayer, singing)
churches.overall_label: Strong Theological Alignment

score_notes.christology: 1689 Confession Chapter 8 — Christ as sole Mediator. Orthodox Christology affirmed.
score_notes.scripture: R44 VALIDATED: Church website confirms 'Eastside Baptist Church holds to the 1689 Second London Baptist Confession.' Chapter 1 — Scripture as sole authority, inerrancy and sufficiency affirmed.
score_notes.mens_discipleship: R44 VALIDATED: Men's Book Study listed under upcoming events. Active men's discipleship confirmed.
score_notes.soteriology: 1689 Reformed soteriology — unconditional election, particular redemption, effectual calling. Doctrines of grace.
score_notes.gender: Age-integrated worship, elder-led by men only. Adopted resolution on women's conscription — explicitly patriarchal position. GREEN — not merely complementarian.
score_notes.leadership: Plurality of elders (Paul Thompson, John Martinez) with deacons (Dan Steineke, Scott Pierce). Biblical elder governance under 1689 Confession.
score_notes.preaching: R44 VALIDATED: Church describes gathering 'to hear the exposition of Scripture' as core purpose. Expository confirmed.
score_notes.mission: Committed to 'advancing the gospel by evangelism, church planting, and shared missionary efforts.' Great Commission focused.
score_notes.cultural: Adopted resolutions on Freemasonry, age-segregation, and women's conscription — engaged with cultural issues from a biblical framework. No compromise.
score_notes.denominational: R44: 1689 Confession affirmed on website; described as 'a local baptistic church.' Confessional accountability confirmed; no formal network affiliation stated but 1689 confessional stance is itself strong accountability.

churches.assessment: Eastside Baptist Church in Twin Falls, Idaho is a 1689 Confessional Reformed Baptist church with a plurality of elders, age-integrated worship, and a robust confessional foundation. Founded in 1972, this church holds to the full 1689 London Baptist Confession including the appendix on baptism. The elder-led structure (Thompson, Martinez) with deacons reflects biblical governance. Their adoption of resolutions on Freemasonry, age-segregation, and women's conscription demonstrates a church willing to take stands on cultural issues from Scripture — not hiding behind neutrality. Men's Book Study and age-integrated model mean men are formed as household leaders, not shuffled into a separate program. Four services per week (Sunday AM, Sunday PM, Sunday School, Wednesday evening) indicates a serious, committed congregation. This is an all-GREEN church — rare and worthy of attention for any Reformed Baptist in the Pacific Northwest.

Charlotte is a thin EFCA metro in the directory, and this is one of the historic anchor congregations for EFCA in NC.

churches.assessment: Escondido URC is a flagship URCNA congregation in North San Diego County, pastored by Rev. Chris Gordon (host of Abounding Grace Radio and a widely recognized voice in confessional Reformed circles). The church holds strictly to the Three Forms of Unity (Belgic Confession, Heidelberg Catechism, Canons of Dort), preaches the Heidelberg Catechism in a second service, and maintains male-only officers. This is textbook confessional Continental Reformed practice — no women in office, no cultural drift, serious catechetical formation for children and adults.

churches.assessment: Fairview Mennonite Church (formerly Fairview Conservative Amish Mennonite) is located four miles north and two miles east of Kalona, Iowa — at the heart of one of the largest Old Order Amish and conservative Mennonite settlements in the Midwest. The congregation traces back to the historic Upper Deer Creek-Fairview Mennonite community. Pastor Conrad has led since September 2016, bringing a remarkable background: born in Delaware, raised on the mission field in northwest Ontario, trained at Moody Bible Institute as a missionary pilot/mechanic, then nine years serving with Mission Aviation Fellowship in Mozambique before being called to Iowa. The CMC/Rosedale Network affiliation provides strong confessional accountability and complementarian polity. Green rating.

churches.pastor_credentials: BA Elizabethtown College, MS South University, MA Liberty University, EdD Eastern University
churches.overall_label: Strong Theological Alignment

score_notes.christology: Trinitarian orthodoxy. Affirms Apostles' Creed. Christ alone for salvation.
score_notes.scripture: Bible as final authority. Adheres to BFC 28 Articles of Faith. High view of Scripture.
score_notes.mens_discipleship: Elder Alex Kocman leads men's discipleship groups at the church. Confirmed by personal relationship with user — Kocman, who writes publicly at American Reformer and Founders Ministries on biblical manhood, carries that conviction into hands-on men's formation inside the local body. Update 2026-09-25: he has publicly said he is preparing to transition to Citylight Church Dover. This note describes his role at Faith until that move is complete.
score_notes.soteriology: Doctrines of grace (TULIP). Salvation by grace through faith alone. Reformed soteriology.
score_notes.gender: Patriarchal household vision, male headship, anti-feminist. Church mission statement is explicitly household-focused: 'joyfully build Christ's kingdom, household by household.' Male-only elders and pastors per BFC bylaws. Elder Alex Kocman is a published voice at American Reformer and Founders Ministries on biblical manhood, male headship, and the missions-critical nature of complementarian/patriarchal order. The church holds a complementarian label but with appropriate biblical-patriarchy guardrails — the hard line on male-only elder rule, an unapologetic household-by-household mission, and Kocman's public writing against the cultural crisis of masculinity — that prevent the usual drift of soft complementarianism into functional egalitarianism. Caveat: church retains a female servant-deacon (Helen Gemmill); by BFC polity deacons 'do not exercise rule or spiritual authority,' so this is a serving role rather than an office of authority.
score_notes.leadership: Elder-led with 3 elders (Senior Pastor + 2). Deacon board for material needs. Denominational accountability through BFC.
score_notes.preaching: Expository, sermon-based teaching through Scripture. Reformed tradition. Podcast sermons available.
score_notes.mission: Church planting emphasis. Elder Alex Kocman directs communications for ABWE (international missions). Bold witness central. Update 2026-09-25: he has publicly said he is staying at ABWE while preparing to serve more closely with Citylight Church Dover.
score_notes.cultural: No DEI/CRT language. Conservative Reformed stance. Family-focused mission statement.
score_notes.denominational: Bible Fellowship Church denomination. Accountable to BFC conference. Self-governing under elder board.

churches.assessment: Faith Bible Fellowship Church of York is a Reformed, evangelical, baptistic church in the BFC denomination. Pastor Wesley Bunting leads a solid elder-governed congregation committed to the doctrines of grace and expository preaching. The church's mission — 'joyfully build Christ's kingdom, household by household' — reflects a patriarchal, family-centered, Great Commission focus. Elder Alex Kocman's role with ABWE, his published work at American Reformer and Founders Ministries, and his hands-on men's discipleship leadership give the church unusually strong DNA on biblical manhood, male headship, and international missions. The one polity detail worth asking about directly: the church retains a female servant-deacon (Helen Gemmill) under BFC's rule that deacons 'do not exercise rule or spiritual authority' — elder rule remains entirely male. Doctrinally and practically, green across the board. Worth visiting. Update 2026-09-25: Elder Alex Kocman has publicly said he and his family are preparing to transition over the coming months to Citylight Church Dover, where he will help lead worship and grow in pastoral ministry. He is staying at ABWE. The elders at Faith are supporting the move. It is not a departure over conflict. Pastor Wesley Bunting remains the shepherd accountable for this church.
churches.gender_detail: Patriarchal household vision, male headship, anti-feminist. Male-only elders (Wesley Bunting, Alex Kocman, Joshua Vann). Female servant-deacon (Helen Gemmill) on board — non-authority role per BFC polity.

churches.assessment: Fellowship Missionary Baptist Church Chicago — known affectionately as "the Ship" — was founded September 10, 1950 by Rev. Dr. Clay Evans (1925-2019), the gospel-and-civil-rights legend whose ministry launched the careers of more than 90 ministers, including Rev. Jesse Louis Jackson Sr., who was ordained at Fellowship in 1968. Evans opened the church's doors to Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. during the Chicago Freedom Movement and helped Jackson launch Operation Breadbasket and later Operation PUSH/Rainbow Coalition from this congregation. Evans served as founding National Board Chairman of Rainbow PUSH 1971-1976. Rev. Charles Jenkins succeeded Evans as Senior Pastor after Evans's December 8, 2000 retirement. Listed for civic/political/civil-rights historical significance.

churches.assessment: First African Baptist Church of Richmond is one of the most historically significant Black churches in the United States — founded in 1841 from the Black members of Richmond's First Baptist Church, at a time when both enslaved and free Black Christians gathered to worship. The church has been a spiritual anchor in Richmond's Black community through slavery, Reconstruction, Jim Crow, and the Civil Rights movement. Dr. Rodney D. Waller is the 10th Senior Pastor, serving for 16+ years and described as an 'anointed' preacher with deep community roots. The theological concerns are the standard ones for NBC/BGAV churches: no formal inerrancy requirement, women in ministry permitted, and the ever-present tension in historically Black mainline churches between prophetic social justice and Gospel proclamation. USMC Ministries should approach with respect for the extraordinary historical legacy while verifying current doctrinal commitments. This church is a kingdom partner candidate for outreach even if full theological alignment is uncertain.

churches.assessment: First Baptist Church Newport News has a remarkable 140-year history on the Virginia Peninsula, organized in 1881 and formally constituted in 1883. Dr. Randy Shepley III leads this historic congregation. The concern is the BGAV affiliation — the Baptist General Association of Virginia is the moderate Baptist body in Virginia, distinct from the more conservative SBC of Virginia. BGAV is connected with the Cooperative Baptist Fellowship and takes a theologically moderate stance that allows greater diversity on Scripture, gender roles, and cultural issues than the SBC's Baptist Faith & Message 2000. This doesn't make FBCNN a bad church — but it means verification is required. Visit, listen to the preaching, ask directly about their stance on Scripture's authority and complementarian convictions before committing. The historic pedigree is impressive; the denominational framework is less clearly conservative.

churches.assessment: First Baptist San Antonio is a historic downtown SBC church (est. ~1861) led by Senior Pastor Chris Johnson. Doctrinally strong: affirms Jesus as co-equal with the Father, Scripture as God's Word and 'supreme and final source of truth,' and salvation as God's free gift through personal faith in Christ. Notable strength: dedicated men's ministry ('Fearlessly Following Jesus') and a unique Bible study integration model where the same passage is studied across all ministries. One concern: women hold 'Minister' titles (Megan Langan, Tera Kouba), which goes beyond traditional complementarian support roles while stopping short of 'Pastor' titles. churches.assessment: President Lyndon B. Johnson considered the First Christian Church in Johnson City TX his "home church." LBJ was baptized in 1923 at age 14 during a Pedernales River revival hosted by this congregation, joining the Christian Church (Disciples of Christ) on the conviction that the Disciples' beliefs aligned with his views (he had been raised in Baptist churches). The congregation was organized in 1903; the original sanctuary stood at 6th & Avenue E and the present church is at 401 E Cypress. Currently a Christian Church (DoC) congregation, reflecting the denomination's 1968 Restructure into mainline polity and subsequent affirming positions. Listed here for civic/political historical significance.

churches.assessment: First Methodist Church of Waco is a historic 1859 congregation that was among the earliest to leave the UMC and join the Global Methodist Church in 2022. Rev. Dr. Mike Voigts became Senior Pastor in May 2025 after serving as a professor at Asbury Theological Seminary — bringing academic Wesleyan depth to the pulpit. The church operates three campuses: the Main Campus on Cobbs Drive, the Speegleville Campus, and a Baylor Campus specifically reaching university students with a Tuesday 7 PM service. One flag worth noting: Rev. Dr. Blossom Matthews serves as Senior Associate Pastor, meaning this particular GMC church does appoint women to pastoral roles (distinct from formal elder ordination, which varies by conference). This places the church closer to the YELLOW end of the gender-rubric for readers committed to male-only ordination. For those comfortable with women in teaching/associate roles but male senior leadership, it's a solid orthodox Wesleyan option in Central Texas.

Jack's background is notable: 13 years as a NJ State Trooper, 12 years as Director of Camp Edge, business owner, doctorate from Seton Hall, and Deacon studies at Palmer Theological Seminary. churches.assessment: First United Methodist Church in Midland, Texas was founded in 1885 — the first congregation organized in Midland. On November 5, 1977, 31-year-old future President George W. Bush married 31-year-old Laura Welch at this church's Glass Memorial Chapel; the Glass Chapel was completed in 1976, just a year before the wedding. The Bush wedding gives this church its primary national notability. Current senior pastor is Dr. Tim Walker, with Rev. Kurt Borden as associate. Like Highland Park UMC Dallas, First Methodist Midland stayed within the post-2024 United Methodist Church after the conservative Global Methodist Church disaffiliation wave. Per MOOP rubric this is RED at the denominational level given the post-2024 UMC departure from biblical authority on sexual ethics. Included for situational awareness about the wedding site of a former president and first lady.

churches.assessment: Forefront Church is a contemporary non-denominational congregation in Virginia Beach led by Lead Pastor Jason Bedell. The church has a seeker-friendly posture — 'Everybody's Welcome, Nobody's Perfect, Anything's Possible' — and offers accessibility for those exploring faith. Red flags for men seeking doctrinal depth: the church lists 'Social Justice' as a program category, which warrants investigation into how gospel and social concern are balanced. No explicit statement of faith was accessible via web research. Jason Bedell's passion for reaching unchurched people is evident, but the theological rigor and elder governance structure are unknown. Forefront would require a direct visit and conversation with pastoral staff to evaluate. Not an automatic red — but requires due diligence for men prioritizing theological substance.

churches.assessment: Fredericksburg Baptist Church is one of the older Baptist congregations in the city, located on historic Princess Anne Street. The mission language is straightforwardly Christ-centered — 'on mission together, striving to continue the work of Christ' with commitments to 'the praise of God and the proclamation of the word of God' and 'the preservation, instruction, and spreading of the Gospel.' That's a healthy public-facing posture. The honest concern is BGAV affiliation: the Baptist General Association of Virginia is the moderate Virginia Baptist stream, separate from SBC, and the denominational structure allows women in pastoral roles and leans progressive on several fronts. Pastor David Haun's theological convictions are unknown. Before visiting, Moop should confirm the church's stance on Scripture inerrancy, women in ministry, and elder accountability. The Princess Anne address is prime downtown Fredericksburg — a historic congregation worth investigating. (Also operates as "FXBG Baptist Church" with shorter URL/branding via fxbgbaptist.org.)

churches.assessment: Fredericksburg Church of Christ has a lot going for it: high Scripture authority, Trinitarian orthodoxy, complementarian leadership with male elder plurality, expository DNA, and no cultural drift indicators. The congregation explicitly states they are 'not a denomination, but simply Christians that belong to the body of believers of which Christ is the head' — that's a healthy posture. The hard stop for a faith-alone evangelical like Moop: Churches of Christ traditionally teach that baptism is necessary for salvation, not merely a sign of it. This is the theological fault line that separates the Restoration Movement from mainstream evangelicalism — and it's a real one. Not a cult, not heresy in the broad sense, but incompatible with sola fide. Worth a conversation with leadership to clarify their exact position on baptism and salvation before getting deeper. Some congregations in this tradition have moved toward a more grace-emphasis soteriology; some have not.

churches.assessment: Fredericksburg Full Gospel Fellowship is the most prominent charismatic/Full Gospel church in downtown Fredericksburg proper, meeting at 708 Prince Edward Street. "Full Gospel" signals an emphasis on all the gifts of the Holy Spirit — tongues, prophecy, healing — and Spirit-baptism theology. The church presents as non-denominational, community-oriented, and doctrinally evangelical in its core gospel message ("To know Him, and to make Him known"). Two Sunday services (10AM and 6:30PM) suggests a committed congregation. However, the lack of a named pastor on the website is a yellow flag for accountability. For a man with solid complementarian convictions and a high-church theology of Scripture, a charismatic/Full Gospel environment warrants investigation before commitment. Not a hard no — but visit before joining.

churches.assessment: Fredericksburg Presbyterian Church on Princess Anne Street is a historic congregation with over 200 years of ministry in the city — that heritage is real and worth noting. However, it affiliates with the Presbyterian Church (USA), which formally departed from biblical authority in 2015 by voting to approve same-sex marriage, ordains women at all levels of church government, and does not affirm biblical inerrancy. The church's website language about 'preserving God's creation' and 'honoring gifts' suggests alignment with the denomination's progressive trajectory. For a man committed to complementarian Christianity, biblical inerrancy, and historic sexual ethics, PCUSA is a disqualifying affiliation. This entry serves as a reference so men visiting downtown Fredericksburg understand why this historic church, despite its beautiful building and heritage, is not the right choice theologically.

score_notes.preaching: OPC pulpits are characterized by expository, Christ-centered, Law/Gospel preaching from the Westminster tradition.
score_notes.mens_discipleship: OPC congregations typically emphasize family worship, catechism instruction, and male headship in home and church — strong formation pipeline for men.
score_notes.mission: OPC Committee on Foreign Missions and Home Missions actively plants confessionally Reformed churches domestically and abroad.

churches.assessment: Grace Bible Church is a multi-campus non-denominational church established in Virginia Beach in 1992, now operating in Lynnhaven, Norfolk, and expanding to Strawbridge. Co-lead pastors Eric Sanzone and Matt Breitenberg lead a church with clear community engagement focus. The church's 'FOR the 757' branding emphasizes being FOR families, racial unity, recovery, and schools — language that can reflect either genuine gospel-centered concern or CRT-influenced social justice priorities. This distinction requires in-person investigation. A female Executive Director of NextGen on the leadership team suggests some role for women in ministry leadership; the extent of this requires direct inquiry. Grace Bible has the infrastructure of a healthy community church. Men seeking theological precision should request the statement of faith and evaluate preaching quality before committing.

churches.assessment: Grace Bible Church in Wappingers Falls, NY is one of the most significant anti-social-justice evangelical churches in America. Senior Pastor Scott Harris and his son Jon Harris (Music Director) lead a congregation explicitly committed to biblical manhood, expository preaching, and cultural resistance. Jon Harris hosts the Conversations That Matter podcast — a leading voice against woke Christianity, CRT, egalitarianism, and denominational drift. He is the author of Social Justice Goes to Church and Against All Who Dwell on the Earth. Annual Music and Masculinity Conference. The family-integrated, patriarchal, Bible-centered culture makes this one of the rare GREEN-rated churches in New York state. Only yellow mark is independence (no external denominational accountability), but the internal culture is strongly orthodox.

churches.assessment: Grace Church Lynchburg is an Evangelical Free Church of America congregation with 35+ years of faithful ministry in the Lynchburg/Madison Heights corridor. Founded in 1988, Grace Church has served through six rented facilities and is now building a permanent home across from its current meeting place at Monelison Middle School — a sign of a congregation committed to long-term community investment. The EFCA is one of the strongest evangelical networks for theological accountability: clear confessional statement on inerrancy, male-only senior pastors, Great Commission mission, and strong doctrinal formation. For a man in the Madison Heights/Lynchburg area wanting a smaller, community-embedded church with solid evangelical credentials, Grace Church EFCA is worth visiting.
