churches.assessment: Grace Community Church is a 1997 church-plant of Trinity Presbyterian — making it a second-generation PCA congregation in Charlottesville with strong theological roots. Rev. Jon Anderson leads a church explicitly committed to Reformed doctrine, the authority of Scripture, and Great Commission discipleship. The PCA framework means complementarian leadership, inerrancy, and faith-alone salvation are non-negotiable doctrinal positions — not cultural preferences. For any man seeking a doctrinally serious Reformed congregation in the greater Charlottesville area, Grace Community offers all the theological strength of Trinity in a potentially smaller, more intimate setting.

churches.assessment: Grace Community Church in Chesapeake is a small-to-medium non-denominational congregation led by Pastor Stephen Hildebrandt. The church distinguishes itself in Hampton Roads by its commitment to expository teaching — chapter by chapter, verse by verse, precept upon precept. This is one of the strongest indicators of a healthy teaching church. The home fellowship model (Sunday afternoon gatherings in homes throughout Chesapeake) reflects a shepherding culture that goes beyond Sunday-only programming. Hildebrandt's personal testimony — an aerospace engineer who came to Christ and found his calling in ministry — suggests depth and earnest faith. Key unknowns: formal statement of faith, elder gender policy, and church accountability structure. For men in Chesapeake who want a teaching church with real community, GCC deserves serious investigation. The expository approach and home fellowship culture set it apart from most Hampton Roads options.

churches.assessment: Grace Covenant Presbyterian Church Williamsburg is a PCA congregation serving the Williamsburg/James City County area — bringing the full weight of PCA Reformed accountability to the Peninsula. The Presbyterian Church in America is one of the theologically strongest Reformed denominations in evangelical Christianity: Westminster Confession of Faith and Catechisms, male-only ordained ministry, expository preaching tradition, and active missions through MTW and Reformed University Fellowship. The Williamsburg context (College of William & Mary nearby) creates natural opportunities for campus engagement. PCA churches are consistently among the most doctrinally sound options in any geographic area. For a man on the Peninsula wanting Reformed evangelical accountability and confessional worship, Grace Covenant PCA is a top-tier option.

churches.assessment: Grace Episcopal Church is the historic home parish of President Gerald R. Ford and Betty Ford, who were married in the old sanctuary in 1948 and whose private funeral was held here in 2006. The parish remains beautiful and historic, with strong choral and liturgical traditions in the Episcopal style. However, for the MOOP rubric, Grace is firmly within The Episcopal Church (TEC) — a denomination that since 1976 has ordained women to all orders, since 2003 has consecrated openly gay bishops, and since 2015 has authorized same-sex marriage rites. These denominational positions place Grace at red on cultural, gender, and denominational dimensions of the rubric. The parish is in a season of transition following the 2024 dissolution-by-merger of the Episcopal Diocese of Western Michigan into the new Diocese of the Great Lakes. Beautiful history. Significant theological distance from MOOP's confessional commitments.

churches.assessment: Grace Reformed Church is a historic Washington DC congregation with a fascinating history — it was the church of President Theodore Roosevelt during his time in the White House. Originally an Evangelical and Reformed Church congregation, it merged into the United Church of Christ (UCC) in 1957. Today the UCC is one of the most theologically liberal denominations in America, fully affirming LGBTQ+ clergy and same-sex marriage, rejecting biblical inerrancy, and embracing pluralistic soteriology. Individual UCC congregations vary in their degree of liberalism, but the denomination provides no orthodox accountability. The historic building and Roosevelt connection make it interesting from a historical standpoint, but for a man seeking biblically sound Word ministry and gospel-centered community, Grace Reformed DC is not recommended. Seek out Reformed churches in the area that have maintained confessional integrity.

churches.assessment: Grantham Church is the historic flagship of the Brethren in Christ U.S. denomination, founded near the campus of what is now Messiah University in Mechanicsburg, Pennsylvania. Pastor David Flowers brings a serious academic-pastoral pedigree — biblical studies graduate degrees, 25+ years across Texas, Virginia, and Pennsylvania, and a published trajectory in New Testament studies and early Christian ethics. The Brethren in Christ tradition holds together Anabaptist peace witness with Wesleyan-Holiness soteriology and pietist devotion — a hybrid that produces mission-minded, Bible-loving congregations but with synergistic rather than Reformed soteriology. For a Mechanicsburg-area man wanting a Christ-centered, mission-oriented church with a graduate-degreed expositor in the pulpit, Grantham deserves a careful look. The denominational yellow flag is gender — BIC USA does permit women's ordination at congregational discretion, though Grantham's senior pastoral office is male.

churches.assessment: Greater Tabernacle Missionary Baptist (Lawrenceburg TN) called Rev. Shonda Reynolds Christian as senior pastor in June 2015 and was disfellowshipped by the Lawrence County Association of Baptists by a 73-4 vote on October 12, 2015 — the association explicitly citing the Baptist Faith and Message 2000 Article VI ('the office of pastor is limited to men as qualified by Scripture'). Pastor Christian, who continues to lead the church a decade later, publicly characterized the disfellowship as 'unchristian' and challenged the binding force of the 2000 BF&M revision. This case set the early modern precedent for SBC state-association action against churches with female senior pastors and remains the longest-running Mid-South case.

churches.enrichment_notes:
Earliest modern Mid-South precedent for state-association disfellowship of an SBC-cooperating church over a female senior pastor. Pastor Christian's tenure has now exceeded a decade, making this an enduring drift case rather than a transient one.

churches.assessment: Harrisburg Brethren in Christ Church is a city-center congregation under Pastor Hank Johnson, who came up through this very church — first as Youth Pastor (2008), then Pastor of Discipleship & Youth (2013), and finally Senior Pastor (November 2018). His backstory is striking: born in Monrovia, Liberia, he and his family lived as immigrants and refugees through Sierra Leone and Côte d'Ivoire before settling in Palisades Park, NJ and Philadelphia. His MDiv and his work on the BIC Historical Society board and as Atlantic Conference assistant moderator suggest a serious denominational pastor. For a Harrisburg-area man wanting a Bible-rooted, urban, mission-oriented church under male senior leadership in the Anabaptist-Holiness tradition, Harrisburg BIC merits a careful visit. Denominational yellow on gender remains because BIC USA permits women's ordination.

churches.assessment: Hayes Barton Baptist (Raleigh NC) is a 1926-founded congregation dual-aligned with the Baptist State Convention of NC (SBC's NC state convention) and the Cooperative Baptist Fellowship. The senior pulpit is occupied by Dr. David J. Hailey (male), but two ordained women carry the formal title 'Pastor' on staff — Rev. Kristen Muse as Executive Pastor (since 2011) and Rev. Sarah Mears as Associate Pastor of Children and Families and Communication. Muse was interviewed in 2024 specifically as an example of a female SBC pastor whose role would be banned under the Law Amendment that subsequently failed. The use of 'Pastor' (not 'Minister') in formal staff titling places the congregation in direct conflict with BF&M 2000 Article VI while remaining nominally SBC-cooperating.

churches.enrichment_notes: Live SBC.net directory listing as of 2025; female pastors with explicit 'Pastor' titling. Distinct from the existing 'First Baptist Church Raleigh NC' black-rated record at 99 N Salisbury St — Hayes Barton is at 1800 Glenwood Ave in the Five Points neighborhood.

churches.assessment: Heights Church is a fast-growing non-denominational congregation in the Henrico/West End Richmond area, affiliated with ARC (Association of Related Churches) — a charismatic church-planting network. The church runs three Sunday services and has a significant following. The core disqualifier for USMC Ministries alignment is the co-pastor structure: Josh and Crystal Whitlow are both listed as 'Pastors' in ARC promotional materials, representing a fully egalitarian leadership model incompatible with complementarian theology. ARC churches also tend toward charismatic, experiential, and seeker-sensitive frameworks that prioritize emotional engagement over expository rigor. Visitor reviews confirm the preaching is Christ-centered and practical, which is positive, but the gender/leadership structure alone is disqualifying for any man committed to male-only pastoral leadership. Not recommended as a home church for theologically conservative men.

The church describes itself as 'a church family of broken people under God's grace who make disciples of Jesus Christ' — language that signals gospel-centeredness. churches.assessment: High Street Baptist Church is a historic BBFI (Baptist Bible Fellowship International) flagship congregation in Springfield, MO — the BBFI's home city and the location of Baptist Bible College and the BBFI Mission Office. Founded 1953, the congregation has been a center of moderate IFB practice within the BBFI stream, generally KJV-preferred (rather than hard Ruckmanite KJV-Only), with strong missions emphasis through BBFI's globally active mission office. Patriarchal leadership and complementarian household structure are presumed by BBFI default. Visit with discernment to confirm KJV position (preferred-traditional vs. hard KJV-Only) and cultural engagement.

churches.assessment: Highland Park United Methodist Church is a large historic Dallas UMC congregation (founded 1916) at 3300 Mockingbird Lane. George W. Bush was an active member 1989-1995 and volunteered in a ministry serving low-income Hispanic families during those years; the church is currently constructing the President George W. and Laura Bush Family Confirmation Center on the Mockingbird Campus. Rev. Paul Rasmussen served as senior minister 2013-2026 and stepped down due to Parkinson's disease; Rev. Matt Tuggle became senior minister in 2026. Highland Park is institutionally part of the post-2024 United Methodist Church, which removed "incompatibility" language around homosexuality and opened LGBTQ+ ordination and same-sex marriage at the 2024 General Conference. Conservative UMC congregations departed during the 2022-2024 disaffiliation window to form the Global Methodist Church (GMC); Highland Park stayed UMC. Per MOOP rubric this is RED at the denominational level even if the local congregation is among the more traditional UMC megachurches. Included for situational awareness about a former president's home church.
churches.denomination_detail: Post-2024 UMC — stayed with the denomination after the conservative GMC departure window.

churches.assessment: Historic First Baptist Church of Beech Island is an 1832-founded SBC-affiliated Baptist congregation in the Aiken / North Augusta area. Watson as interim or successor. Per primary-source report from MOOP Directory editor Adam Johns (who knows Williams personally), Williams was asked to resign and given severance over biblically-sound, orthodoxically-defensible conservative views the congregation's leadership found unwelcome. The church's published statement of faith claims subscription to both BF&M 2000 and the 1646 LBCF — an unusually strong confessional claim — but is silent on women in ministry, marriage, and sexuality. The combination of (a) a conservative pastor being asked to step down despite holding orthodox views, (b) confessional-claim silence on the disputed-third-rail issues of the moment, and (c) confused dual-confession citation suggests a posture more 'institutional-historic' than 'confessionally-orthodox.' score_notes.christology: Orthodox Trinitarian; affirms Apostles/Nicene Creed (Eastern form, without filioque).
score_notes.scripture: Scripture + Holy Tradition co-authoritative; Seven Ecumenical Councils authoritative.
score_notes.soteriology: Eastern Orthodox soteriology is theosis (deification) with synergism — humans cooperate with divine grace. Not Protestant sola fide; no Reformation justification-by-faith-alone framework.
score_notes.gender: Male-only priests; Theotokos (Mother of God) and icon veneration.
score_notes.leadership: Apostolic succession; bishop-priest-deacon structure with synodical oversight.
score_notes.preaching: Homilies tied to liturgical cycle — not expository in Protestant sense.
score_notes.mission: Active OCA parish in growing Northern Virginia corridor.
score_notes.cultural: OCA is English-language American Orthodox jurisdiction; less ethnic-ghetto than Greek/Russian.
score_notes.denominational: OCA affiliation confirmed via domain (holytrinity-oca.org) and site branding. Liturgical cycle (Divine Liturgy, Great Vespers, seasonal fasts/feasts, sacramental 'mysteries') all confirmed — classic Eastern Orthodox distinctives. RED overall rating on sola fide grounds retained.

churches.assessment: Holy Trinity Reston is an English-language OCA parish serving the Reston/Ashburn Northern Virginia corridor under Fr. Paul Harrilchak. OCA (Orthodox Church in America) is the most Americanized Orthodox jurisdiction and conducts services in English. Eastern Orthodox red-flag on soteriology: theosis/synergism, not Protestant sola fide; Scripture + Holy Tradition co-authoritative; icon and Theotokos veneration. Full apostolic succession and Nicene Trinitarian orthodoxy preserved.

churches.assessment: HOPE Church (House of Prayer for Everyone) in Clarksville, MD is an ECO (Evangelical Covenant Order Presbyterian) congregation built around a house church model. Every member is integrated into a weekly house church gathering for dinner, fellowship, prayer, and Scripture — with corporate Sunday worship. ECO was formed in 2012 as a theologically conservative alternative to the PCUSA, affirming the Westminster Confession and biblical gender theology. This church's approach — Scripture-centered, prayer-saturated, community-integrated — reflects healthy early church patterns (Acts 2:42-46). For a man in the DC/Maryland area wanting deep discipleship, genuine community, and doctrinally sound Reformed theology, HOPE Church is a strong recommendation. The house church structure particularly builds the kind of accountable brotherhood that produces mature men.

churches.assessment: Huguenot Road Baptist is a Chesterfield County congregation serving the southwest Richmond area. Led by Dr. Robert E. Lee IV, the church emphasizes community and biblical engagement. The pastor's weekly letters touch on faith and current events, indicating an engaged shepherd. Standard BGAV concerns apply — moderate denomination that separated from SBC over inerrancy and gender. Dr. Lee's doctorate and consistent pastoral communication suggest a serious minister, but his theological positions on inerrancy, complementarianism, and soteriology need direct confirmation before recommending. A visit and conversation with Dr. Lee would quickly reveal whether this church holds conservative convictions within a moderate denomination.

churches.assessment: Immanuel Baptist is one of Richmond's historic congregations, established in 1852 and located on the storied Monument Avenue corridor. Lead Pastor Jordan Fanara describes himself as committed to 'shepherding through sound, biblical preaching' and passionate about 'introducing lost souls to Jesus' — language consistent with evangelical, Great Commission conviction. The church's public-facing posture is warm and Word-centered. The honest concern is BGAV affiliation: the Baptist General Association of Virginia is the moderate Virginia Baptist stream that separated from the SBC in the 1990s over inerrancy and gender. Jordan Fanara's educational background (B.S. Education + M.A. Pastoral Counseling) is practical but doesn't signal strong Reformed or conservative Baptist theological training. Before committing, verify stance on Scripture inerrancy, women in ministry, and elder accountability. Immanuel has the posture worth visiting.

churches.assessment: Immanuel Bible Church is a gem in Northern Virginia. Founded 1964, it's served the Springfield area for over 60 years with a consistent commitment to Scripture. Teaching Pastor Jesse Johnson is Dean of The Master's Seminary Washington DC campus — that's John MacArthur's seminary, and it means the preaching at IBC will be expository, word-saturated, and doctrinally serious. IBC also hosts a Hispanic congregation, which is a mark of genuine community engagement. For a man who wants a smaller-to-mid-size church with rigorous biblical preaching, discipleship infrastructure (small groups emphasized), and a clear theological north star — IBC is an excellent choice in the NoVA corridor.

churches.assessment: Indian Valley Faith Fellowship in Harleysville, Pennsylvania has been led by Senior Pastor Dean Landry since July 2014, after his 16+ years of pastoral ministry at a church in Northern Michigan. Pastor Landry holds a B.A. from Baptist Bible College of PA and two graduate degrees — from Bethel College and Grand Rapids Theological Seminary. Family Pastor Nate Paine fills out the multi-pastor team. The Alliance of Mennonite Evangelical Congregations (AMEC) represents the conservative Anabaptist-evangelical body that broke from Mennonite Church USA in 2002 over doctrinal and sexuality concerns — its two-fold confessional commitment is to evangelical orthodoxy and historic biblical Anabaptism. For a Montgomery County or Harleysville-area man wanting a complementarian, biblically-grounded, Anabaptist-pietist church with a graduate-degreed expository pastor, Indian Valley Faith Fellowship is a strong candidate.

churches.assessment: Kessler Park UMC is an explicitly and proudly LGBTQ+-affirming congregation in the Oak Cliff neighborhood of Dallas. The About page openly states the church is 'United Methodist in tradition, progressive in theology,' takes 'the Bible seriously, but not literally,' and is 'a proud member of the Reconciling Ministries Network.' The home page tagline ('A reconciling community of hope') and a prominent rainbow logo make the posture unambiguous. The church stayed in the post-2024 United Methodist Church through the disaffiliation window — the wing that formally removed restrictions on same-sex marriage and LGBTQ+ ordination at the 2024 General Conference. Pastoral team includes lead pastor Eric Folkerth (a self-described 'activist'), children's minister Kay Ash, and congregational care minister Ken Kelley. The directory user's tip of 'apostate, steer people away' is consistent with what the church openly publishes about itself: a progressive-mainline framework that has formally abandoned biblical authority on sexual ethics. Not recommended for men seeking a complementarian, inerrancy-affirming, Great-Commission-centered congregation.

churches.gender_detail: AoG ordains women per General Council polity. Default YELLOW gender; verify local senior pastor's gender + congregation's actual practice. Joel Osteen senior pastor; wife Victoria Osteen co-pastor (teaching role).

score_notes.christology: Affirms Trinity and deity of Christ on About page, but Christ functionally framed as enabler of personal flourishing rather than crucified-and-risen Lord.
score_notes.scripture: Affirms Bible authority on paper; in practice teaching consistently extracts inspirational fragments without exegetical context.
score_notes.soteriology: Prosperity-gospel framework: 'Your Best Life Now' theology shifts gospel from sin/atonement to favor/declaration. Salvation present but eclipsed by self-actualization narrative.
score_notes.preaching: Hallmark prosperity-gospel preaching: declarations, seed-faith, 'God wants you to prosper' as the recurring frame. Cross/repentance largely absent.
score_notes.gender: AoG-polity female ordination available; Victoria Osteen functions as co-pastor with frequent platform teaching role. YELLOW per AoG default plus complementarian variance.
score_notes.sexuality: Has historically declined to take a public stance on LGBTQ matters in either direction; Osteen's repeated 'I don't know' interview answers are well-documented. Functionally non-affirming in liturgy but ambiguous publicly.
score_notes.race: Multiethnic congregation in Houston; no specific concerns flagged.
score_notes.polity: AoG affiliated but functions as personality-led independent megachurch with limited denominational accountability visible.
score_notes.cultural: Maximally seeker-sensitive, therapeutic moralistic deism overlap, light political footprint.
score_notes.scandal: Victoria Osteen 2014 'do good for yourself' viral clip; 2014 plumber-discovered hidden cash in church wall (later subject of theft investigation); ongoing seed-faith fundraising controversies.

score_notes.scripture: Homepage 'stand on the truth of God's Word' — affirmation present but inerrancy depth not surfaced.
score_notes.gender: No explicit statement on male-only eldership found; non-denominational multi-campus context raises questions about complementarian accountability.
score_notes.leadership: References 'Our Pastors & Leadership' but no individual elders surfaced. Multi-campus video-driven model. Held yellow.
score_notes.preaching: Multi-campus typically uses video preaching from central location; campus pastor supplements. Tends toward topical/applicational.
score_notes.mens_discipleship: No dedicated men's ministry confirmed — large churches of this type often have life groups but not masculine discipleship focus.
score_notes.denominational: No external network affiliation found; no ARC red flag found either. Self-governing. Held yellow.
score_notes.christology: 'Truth of God's Word and the life-changing power of Jesus Christ'; Easter messaging 'He is still the King' — Christ-centered framing but explicit Trinity/creed not on public page.
score_notes.soteriology: Conversion-focused theology with dedicated 'Salvation' section in Next Steps; mission brings 'people far from God' into 'a full life in Christ' — evangelical soteriology.
score_notes.mission: 'Point people to life in Jesus through love, truth, and purpose'; leading 'people far from God into a Full Life in Christ.'
score_notes.cultural: Welcoming, accessible language ('whether you're looking for a church to call home or are just ready to try something new'); six-campus multi-site model with pragmatic contextualization.

churches.assessment: Lifepoint Church is the largest evangelical multi-campus operation in the Fredericksburg area, meeting at 1400 Central Park Blvd with three Sunday services. With six locations across Virginia and Kentucky, Lifepoint has infrastructure, resources, and a clear evangelical mission: "lead people far from God into a full life in Christ." Campus pastor Daniel leads a strong local team. However, Lifepoint exhibits the typical hallmarks of the large seeker-friendly non-denominational model: polished production, unclear doctrinal standards on gender/leadership, video preaching likely from a central teaching team, and life-group-driven community rather than classical discipleship. The mission is solid; the theological depth and complementarian backbone need verification. A man looking for a doctrinally rigorous, male-formation-focused church should visit with those specific questions in hand.
churches.gender_detail: No public statement on male-only eldership; multi-campus non-denom model typically non-complementarian or uncommitted
churches.denomination_detail: Independent evangelical multi-site (six campuses across Virginia and Kentucky); no denominational affiliation mentioned.

churches.assessment: Lutheran Church of Our Savior is the ELCA Lutheran congregation on Lejeune Boulevard — the main road between downtown Jacksonville NC and Camp Lejeune. The pastor, Mike Lang, is male, and the congregation likely contains many sincere Christians (including military families). But the denominational frame is the issue. ELCA's 2009 ChurchWide Assembly formally authorized the ordination of partnered same-sex clergy and the blessing of same-sex relationships; subsequent assemblies expanded that posture. ELCA has ordained women at all levels (including bishops) since 1970. The homepage greeting — "ALL are welcome" with open communion ("Holy Communion is available to all baptized Christians") — is consistent with the inclusive/welcoming identity ELCA has cultivated. This is institutional drift from biblical sexual ethics. Per MOOP rubric, ELCA congregations are flagged RED at the denominational level regardless of local pastor or local rhetorical conservatism. If Adam visited a Lutheran church near MCAS New River during V-22 training, this is the most visible Lutheran congregation on the Camp Lejeune corridor. Not recommended for MOOP-aligned theological convictions.

Confirm new lead pastor identity before personal outreach.

The denominational gender yellow flag remains as a structural caveat; the local senior pastor is male.

churches.assessment: Maranatha Baptist Church in Plains, Georgia is the small-town Baptist congregation where President Jimmy Carter taught Sunday school for nearly four decades — from 1981 until his health declined in 2019. The church drew international visitors who came specifically to hear Carter teach; he funeralized there in January 2025. Rev. Tony Lowden was Carter's personal pastor and the first Black lead pastor, succeeded by Rev. Ashley Guthas in 2024 — the church's first woman pastor (a divorced mother of two). In March 2025 under Guthas the church removed American flags from the sanctuary. Maranatha is independent / CBF-aligned (Cooperative Baptist Fellowship, formed 1991 by ex-SBC moderates over biblical-inerrancy and women-in-ministry questions). Carter himself publicly broke with the SBC over its 2000 BFM revision restricting women from senior pastor roles. Per MOOP rubric the female-senior-pastor + CBF-progressive denominational posture is RED on gender / leadership; included for situational awareness about the most famous lay-led Bible-teaching church in America under Carter.

churches.assessment: Marble Collegiate Church is one of America's most historically significant Reformed congregations, with roots back to 1628 and the current Marble building dedicated in 1854. Norman Vincent Peale served as pastor from 1932 to 1984, building a half-century legacy of positive-thinking preaching that profoundly shaped a young Donald Trump — whose family attended faithfully during his childhood and whose first wedding Peale officiated. Today Marble is led by Rev. Dr. Michael Bos and is openly LGBT-affirming, rejects biblical inerrancy in favor of historical-critical hermeneutics, performs same-sex weddings, and participates annually in NYC Pride. Dual-affiliated with the RCA and the UCC — both progressive mainlines, with the UCC being the most theologically progressive mainline in America. This is RED on the MOOP rubric; included for situational awareness about the formative church of a sitting president.

churches.assessment: Martinsburg Brethren in Christ Church sits in central Pennsylvania's Allegheny Conference of the BIC. Pastor Michael Abell — Canadian-born with deep BIC roots on both sides of his family and 25 years in BIC ministry — has been Lead Pastor here for some time. The Brethren in Christ tradition combines Anabaptist peace heritage with Wesleyan-Holiness soteriology, producing a congregation type that's mission-oriented and Bible-loving but theologically synergistic rather than Reformed. For a Bedford or Blair County man wanting a settled, denominationally-rooted church under male senior leadership in the Anabaptist-Holiness stream, Martinsburg BIC is worth a visit. The denominational yellow flag remains because BIC USA permits women's ordination at the congregational level, though this congregation's lead pastor is male.

Theologically, this is one of the strongest finds in Batch 3: an explicitly SBC-affiliated church (confirmed by Wikipedia) with a rock-solid doctrinal statement affirming full biblical inerrancy, Great Commission centrality, and Trinitarian orthodoxy. The stated mission — 'reach people with the good news of Jesus Christ and lead them into a strong relationship with Him' — is clean evangelicalism. The current absence of a named pastor in public directories is a yellow flag — worth confirming pastoral leadership status by phone before visiting. Strong candidate for the list.

churches.assessment: Mennonite Christian Fellowship (MCF) — the namesake congregation of the small conservative Anabaptist denomination — is located in Atmore, Alabama. The MCF denomination originated in 1958 from early Amish revivalist groups in Holmes County, Ohio, and now numbers approximately 34 congregations and 1,500+ members nationwide. MCF practices plain dress, women's head covering, plural minister polity (bishop/minister/deacon), male-only ordination, and adheres to the Dordrecht Confession. churches.assessment: Montgomery Brethren in Christ Church serves the Mercersburg area in Franklin County, Pennsylvania, a small rural congregation under Pastor Japheth Nell. Montgomery is one of dozens of Brethren in Christ churches in south-central Pennsylvania, the historic homeland of the BIC tradition. The Brethren in Christ blend Anabaptist peace heritage with Wesleyan-Holiness soteriology and 19th-century pietism — a tradition that produces mission-oriented, Bible-loving congregations though synergistic rather than Reformed. For a Mercersburg or Greencastle man wanting a small, settled, denominationally-rooted Anabaptist-Holiness church, Montgomery BIC is worth investigating. Denominational yellow flag stands because BIC USA permits women's ordination.

churches.assessment: Mt. Bethel Church Marietta GA is one of the most prominent post-UMC independent megachurches. Senior Pastor Dr. Jody Ray (since 2016) was reassigned by UMC Bishop Sue Haupert-Johnson in 2021; he surrendered his UMC clergy credentials in protest, the congregation gathered ~4,700 signatures, and the church ultimately paid ~$13.1M in a 2022 settlement to leave the UMC with property. Importantly, Mt. Bethel did NOT join the GMC — it operates as an independent Methodist congregation. ~10,000 members, 2,300+ avg attendance. The pastor's and congregation's deliberate stand against UMC progressive leadership is theologically substantive. Yellow denominational reflects post-schism independence with no connectional accountability — the autonomy is sometimes a weakness, sometimes a strength.

churches.assessment: Mt. Horeb Church in Lexington, SC was South Carolina's largest United Methodist congregation before a dramatic 97% congregational vote on February 26, 2023 to leave the UMC, with formal GMC membership finalized in August 2023. Senior Pastor Jeff Kersey has led through this transition. The church runs two campuses (East traditional, West contemporary) with four services total each Sunday morning, and emphasizes making, maturing, and mobilizing disciples. Like all post-2022 GMC churches, the institutional commitment to orthodoxy (evidenced by the costly decision to leave UMC property and structure) is the strongest signal — these are congregations that paid a price to preserve biblical teaching on marriage and Christian doctrine. The GMC South Carolina Conference position on women as elders should be verified; otherwise this is a solidly orthodox Wesleyan option in the Columbia metro area.

churches.assessment: National City Christian Church is the architectural and ecclesiastical "cathedral" of the Christian Church (Disciples of Christ) — a neoclassical John Russell Pope landmark on Thomas Circle, completed 1930, with stained-glass windows commemorating Presidents James A. Garfield and Lyndon B. Johnson, both Disciples. President Johnson occasionally attended during his presidency and his state funeral was held here on January 25, 1973. The church called The Rev. Stephanie Kendell as its first female senior pastor and president in 2023 — she previously served as 1st Vice-Moderator of the entire denomination. Disciples of Christ as a whole is mainline-progressive: non-inerrantist, egalitarian, with many Open & Affirming congregations and openly affirming LGBT clergy. NCCC publicly aligns with this trajectory. By MOOP's rubric the church is red across gender, cultural, denominational, and preaching dimensions — beautiful building, beautiful presidential history, theological distance significant.

score_notes.scripture: Assemblies of God affirms Scripture inerrancy, but charismatic framework adds extra-biblical 'words of knowledge,' prophecy, and experience-driven spirituality that can compete with Scripture's authority.
score_notes.gender: Assemblies of God historically has allowed women in pastoral roles. NCC's stance on female senior pastors/elders needs individual verification — Batterson is complementarian but AoG doesn't require it.
score_notes.soteriology: AoG affirms faith alone for salvation (sola fide), but may add 'second blessing' / baptism of the Holy Spirit with tongues as normative expectation. Salvation clearly gospel-centered but framework can add layers.
score_notes.preaching: Batterson is a gifted communicator and visionary thinker. However, his style is more topical/narrative than expository. He's an ideas guy and cultural connector, not a verse-by-verse expositor.
score_notes.cultural: NCC operates in the DC political ecosystem and intentionally engages culture — both a strength (marketplace presence) and risk (drift). Language around 'justice' should be evaluated. | MOOP-attendance note: Adam Johns attended NCC many years ago. Historical attendance only — does not extend to current-trajectory endorsement (NCC remains RED-rated for charismatic/Bathersonian "your dream is what God wants" framing per existing assessment). | CONSOLIDATION 2026-04-28: Three duplicate records existed (national-community-church-dc, -dc-2, -dc-3). Merged to this canonical record. Rating elevated from RED to BLACK based on prior dc-2 framing: "Assemblies of God multi-site, Mark Batterson, Revoice-adjacent." NCC has been linked to Side B sympathetic content, prosperity-adjacent "your dream is what God wants" theology, and post-2020 cultural-conformity drift. Adam (MOOP) attended NCC many years ago — historical attendance flagged but does not extend to current-trajectory endorsement.
score_notes.mens_discipleship: NCC has life groups and men's engagement, but no dedicated men's discipleship infrastructure as the primary vehicle.
score_notes.denominational: Assemblies of God — provides accountability, but AoG's charismatic framework introduces tensions around gender roles and extra-biblical spiritual gifts.
score_notes.christology: Assemblies of God affiliation affirms Trinity and Christ's deity per AG Fundamental Truths. NCC homepage does not articulate doctrine specifically; generic Jesus-focused language. Green on denominational default.
score_notes.leadership: Lead Pastor Mark Batterson with Pastor Joel Schmidgall and team; AG affirms women in pastoral ministry (NCC has had female teaching pastors). Single-charismatic-leader-plus-team model — watch for celebrity-pastor dynamic.
score_notes.mission: Mission: 'Bless the Lord. Bless the City. Bless the Nations. Bless the Generations.' — Great Commission framed with 'launching pad for world-changers' language emphasizing cultural influence.

churches.assessment: National Community Church under Mark Batterson is culturally influential, evangelistically aggressive, and Batterson himself is clearly Christ-centered in his books and preaching. NCC is known for meeting in movie theaters, Ebenezers Coffeehouse (their ministry-owned coffee shop), and reaching young professionals in DC. The Assemblies of God affiliation provides structure and accountability. However: AoG's charismatic framework, Batterson's topical preaching style, and the DC-area cultural pressure points are real concerns for a man wanting deep doctrinal formation. Visit with discernment. NCC is a good entry point for unchurched people and city engagement, but may not be the primary spiritual food source for a man wanting expository depth.

churches.assessment: Neon Reformed Presbyterian Church is an Orthodox Presbyterian Church congregation in Neon, Kentucky — deep in Letcher County in the Appalachian coal belt of southeastern Kentucky. This is a rare confessional Reformed presence in a region historically dominated by independent Old Regular Baptist, Free Will Baptist, and Pentecostal churches. The OPC's Presbytery of the Southeast covers southeastern Kentucky (rather than the Presbytery of Ohio). Rev. M. Jay Bennett serves as Pastor. For a man wanting strict-subscription Westminster Standards Presbyterianism in eastern Kentucky's mountains, Neon Reformed is functionally unique — a long-standing Appalachian OPC mission witness.

score_notes.christology: PCA affiliation means full Nicene orthodoxy; Christ as only Savior is foundational.

churches.assessment: New City Fellowship is a downtown Fredericksburg gem hiding in plain sight. A PCA church at 200 Prince Edward St — walking distance from Moop's home area — with a clear expository preaching ministry, cross-cultural Great Commission mission, and the full doctrinal infrastructure of the Presbyterian Church in America behind it. The church website explicitly describes anticipating 'a word from the Lord' each Sunday through biblical preaching ('from every page of Scripture') — that's stated expository DNA, not just a marketing phrase. PCA means: Westminster Standards inerrancy, male-elder plurality with denominational accountability, complementarian polity enforced at the presbytery level, and Reformation soteriology. Rev. Robert M. Becker is a James River Presbytery-ordained pastor. The cross-cultural emphasis ('every nation, tribe, people, and language') ties directly to Matthew 28 and Acts 1:8 — healthy missional framing. The Sunday School model (9:30 AM) signals catechetical depth. If Moop is looking for a theologically robust, downtown, PCA congregation — this is the highest-confidence option found in Batch 4.

churches.assessment: New Hope Baptist Church has served the Hampton, Virginia community for approximately 50+ years, recognized by Congress for its 50th anniversary with documented community ministries including evangelism teams, tutorial programs, and seniors' ministry. The church's community presence and active ministry programs are genuine strengths. As an independent Baptist congregation, however, there is no external denominational accountability or confessional standard — all doctrine, governance, and gender polity is determined internally. The current pastoral leadership needs verification via the church website. For a man in the Hampton/Big Bethel Road area, New Hope Baptist is worth investigating directly: visit, evaluate the preaching, ask about their confession of faith and elder/deacon structure, and assess whether it provides the kind of doctrinally serious environment needed for men's formation.

score_notes.gender: OPC Book of Church Order restricts the offices of teaching elder, ruling elder, and deacon to qualified men only (1 Tim 2–3; Titus 1).

score_notes.cultural: OPC historically resists theological accommodation to cultural pressure — Machen's legacy of confessional fidelity over cultural relevance.
score_notes.denominational: Orthodox Presbyterian Church — founded 1936 by J. Gresham Machen as a confessionally Reformed denomination against Modernism in the PCUSA.
score_notes.preaching: OPC pulpits are characterized by expository, Christ-centered, Law/Gospel preaching from the Westminster tradition.
score_notes.mens_discipleship: OPC congregations typically emphasize family worship, catechism instruction, and male headship in home and church — strong formation pipeline for men.
score_notes.mission: OPC Committee on Foreign Missions and Home Missions actively plants confessionally Reformed churches domestically and abroad.

churches.assessment: New Hope Orthodox Presbyterian Church is a congregation of the Orthodox Presbyterian Church (OPC), the confessional Reformed denomination founded in 1936 by J. Gresham Machen. OPC churches subscribe to the Westminster Confession of Faith and Catechisms, restrict ordained office to qualified men, and practice presbyterian polity with accountability through session, presbytery, and General Assembly. Baseline green rating reflects confessional identity; verify local particulars on the website.

Not recommended given the pattern of leadership failures.

churches.assessment: Northwest Chapel is a Dublin, Ohio Grace Brethren congregation founded by — and still pastored by — Dr. Terry Hofecker since 1985, four decades and counting. He pulls double duty as Grace Theological Seminary faculty, was a volunteer Police Chaplain at the World Trade Center disaster site in fall 2001, and serves as Project Administrator for biblical archaeology excavations at Tel Gezer in Israel. That's the resume of a serious pastor-scholar. The Charis Fellowship — formerly Fellowship of Grace Brethren Churches, renamed in 2017 — holds dispensational evangelical theology with Anabaptist roots: complementarian, biblically-inerrantist, mission-oriented. Two Sunday services (9:15 and 11 AM), recovery ministry, full lifecycle ministry portfolio. For a Dublin or northwest-Columbus-area man wanting a doctrinally stable, scholar-led Grace Brethren church with multi-decade pastoral continuity, Northwest Chapel is one of the strongest options in central Ohio.

churches.assessment: Oak Grove Mennonite Church is the longstanding CMC/Rosedale Network congregation in northeastern Oklahoma's Mayes County. Founder-era pastor Richard Birky served 1942-1947, and in 1944 a house was remodeled as the original church building. The current congregation operates under Pastor Carl Helmuth with approximately 26 members. Despite small size, the 80-year continuous Anabaptist witness in this rural Oklahoma community provides meaningful presence in a region otherwise dominated by Southern Baptist and Pentecostal congregations. CMC/Rosedale male-elder polity and conservative confessional integrity yield a green rating.

churches.overall_label: WARNING! — Egalitarian Trajectory

score_notes.christology: Christ-centered language: 'Christ centers us.' Gospel-centered identity. Affirms Baptist Faith and Message (1963 version — not the stricter 2000 version). Orthodox Christology.
score_notes.scripture: Affirms Baptist Faith and Message 1963 — notably NOT the 2000 revision which strengthened inerrancy and complementarian language. Scripture described as 'authoritative guide' but not 'inerrant.' Yellow for weaker scriptural authority position.
score_notes.gender: RED — Major concern. Pastor Jeff Warren has publicly stated: 'Jesus did not genderize the Great Commission, nor does God dispense spiritual gifts to his children according to sex.' The church states 'Both men and women serve equally alongside each other.' Women serve on Board of Trustees (Laura Dronzek as Personnel Chair), chair standing committees, and hold leadership positions. The church withdrew from the SBC in October 2024 specifically over the SBC's push to restrict female pastors. This is an explicitly egalitarian trajectory — the church left the SBC rather than conform to complementarian standards.
score_notes.leadership: Board of Trustees governance model with Deacons, Church Officers, and standing committees. Senior Pastor Jeff Warren leads with Ken Holden (Deacon Chair) and Ken Stone (Board President). Women serve on Board and chair committees. No elder structure — uses trustee/deacon/committee model.
score_notes.soteriology: Baptist heritage suggests faith-alone soteriology. Gospel-centered language. No works-based indicators.
score_notes.cultural: Large megachurch (10,000 members). Emphasis on 'cultural engagement' as a core value. The decision to leave the SBC over women's ordination signals progressive cultural alignment on gender issues. Verify whether other progressive positions follow.
score_notes.preaching: Unable to verify from website alone. Large megachurch format. Founded 1939 with long Baptist tradition. Verify whether preaching is expository or topical/seeker-sensitive.
score_notes.mission: Strong mission emphasis: 'leading all generations to love Jesus.' Spanish-language ministry. Dallas Baptist Association and Texas Baptists partnership for missions and church planting. Multiple service times. Active outreach.
score_notes.mens_discipleship: Men's ministry programming exists. Green for intentional male discipleship.
score_notes.denominational: Withdrew from SBC in October 2024 over women in ministry issue. Remains affiliated with Texas Baptists (BGCT) and Dallas Baptist Association. BGCT is historically moderate. BF&M 1963 (not 2000) as doctrinal standard. Yellow — reduced accountability after SBC departure.

churches.assessment: Park Cities Baptist Church is a large Dallas megachurch (10,000 members, est. 1939) led by Dr. Jeff Warren since 2010. The church withdrew from the SBC in October 2024 specifically over the convention's push to restrict female pastors — a significant red flag for complementarian evaluation. Pastor Warren has publicly advocated for women in ministry, stating Jesus 'did not genderize the Great Commission.' The church affirms the 1963 Baptist Faith & Message (notably NOT the stricter 2000 version) and states men and women 'serve equally alongside each other.' Women serve on the Board of Trustees and chair standing committees. While the church maintains orthodox Christology, gospel-centered language, and active mission engagement, the explicit egalitarian trajectory places it in the RED category for gender/biblical design. The church remains affiliated with Texas Baptists (BGCT) and Dallas Baptist Association but has reduced denominational accountability after leaving the SBC. Not recommended for men seeking a church with complementarian convictions, but doctrinally sound on core gospel issues.
churches.gender_detail: EGALITARIAN TRAJECTORY. Pastor Jeff Warren publicly advocates women in ministry. Church withdrew from SBC (Oct 2024) over women's ordination restrictions. Women serve on Board of Trustees, chair standing committees. Church states 'Both men and women serve equally alongside each other.' BF&M 1963 (no complementarian language) as doctrinal standard instead of BF&M 2000.

score_notes.leadership: CRISIS: From 2020-2024, Senior Minister Mark Booker at center of disagreements with staff and elders. July 2023 17-page letter from former Associate Minister Michael Balboni alleged toxic culture, muzzling of dissent, denigration of congregants, pastoral-confidentiality violations, and controlling behavior. Three ministers (Long, Kam, Linnell) and two elders (Liu, Assogba) resigned. A Vicinage Council report (July 2024) exonerated Booker but a majority of the ministerial staff refused to sign a letter of affirmation. In June 2024, members voted against affirming Booker as senior pastor.
score_notes.soteriology: Classic evangelical — sola fide, substitutionary atonement.
score_notes.cultural: Congregational conflict has produced an 'us-versus-them' dynamic per Wartburg Watch reporting.
score_notes.denominational: CCCC (Conservative Congregational Christian Conference) — confessional evangelical congregational body. Site 404'd on /about/what-we-believe during this fetch.
score_notes.preaching: Booker remains in pulpit as of fetch attempt; preaching evaluations in secondary sources are mixed due to leadership controversy.
score_notes.mens_discipleship: Pre-crisis programming presumably continued; not surfaced during fetch.
score_notes.mission: Historic Park Street missions heritage (Adoniram Judson preached here; Samuel Francis Smith wrote 'My Country 'Tis of Thee' here); current activity disrupted.

churches.assessment: Park Street Church is a historic evangelical congregation in Boston (since 1809), affiliated with the Conservative Congregational Christian Conference (CCCC). Located at the corner of Park and Tremont Streets. Known for faithful evangelical witness in a liberal New England context. Multiple worship styles from traditional organ to contemporary band. Strong Christian formation emphasis. A rare theologically conservative beacon in Boston.
churches.denomination_detail: CCCC (Conservative Congregational Christian Conference) — NOT UCC. Historic Park Street Church of Boston (Adoniram Judson sent from here).

review_flag.reason: Park Street Church is in an ongoing multi-year leadership crisis (2023-2024). Senior Minister Mark Booker was affirmed by 350-173 vote in Feb 2024 but a subsequent congregational meeting REJECTED the assertion that Booker is not disqualified. Multiple ministers and elders resigned over spiritual-abuse allegations. Status is unstable — any rating issued now will likely be stale within months.

churches.enrichment_notes: Rating downgraded yellow → red on documented accountability crisis, multi-year abuse allegations, and multiple clergy resignations. If Booker is removed or resigns and church restabilizes, rating could return to green.

The Nashville Statement is the post-2017 evangelical line on biblical anthropology, marriage, and sexual ethics — affirming creation order, one-man-one-woman marriage, and biblical sexuality. score_notes.preaching: World-class expository preaching. Begg is widely regarded as one of the finest verse-by-verse preachers alive. Truth For Life broadcasts reach millions.
score_notes.mission: Active missions program. Great Commission centered with global outreach through Truth For Life.
score_notes.mens_discipleship: Men's ministry and discipleship groups available.

churches.assessment: Parkside Church under Alistair Begg is one of the premier expository Bible-teaching churches in America. Begg has preached verse-by-verse through Scripture for over 40 years with unwavering commitment to inerrancy, male headship, and the exclusivity of Christ. Truth For Life radio ministry extends his influence globally. The church is elder-led, missions-minded, and doctrinally rock-solid. A top-tier GREEN church. Note: Begg drew controversy in late 2023 for advising a grandmother to attend a grandchild's transgender wedding — he later clarified his pastoral intent but the incident raised some concerns among discernment circles.

churches.assessment: Passion City Church and Louie Giglio's broader Passion movement have done genuine good in mobilizing young adults for worship and anti-trafficking causes. Giglio has shown some cultural accommodation tendencies and the ministry lacks the doctrinal precision and male-headship emphasis that MOOP values. Not a bad church, but not a GREEN church either. YELLOW — good entry point for young believers but needs stronger expository and patriarchal commitments.

churches.assessment: Passion City Church DC is the DC campus of Passion City Church (Atlanta), led by Ben Stuart as city pastor. Ben Stuart is a compelling teacher with solid biblical scholarship — his book 'Single, Dating, Engaged, Married' demonstrates theological depth and pastoral care. He earned his M.A. in historical theology at Dallas Theological Seminary. Passion City Church originated from the Passion movement (Louie Giglio) which is evangelical and mission-focused. Strengths: gifted communicator, strong young adult/college ministry, passion for global missions. Cautions: multi-site model disperses local eldership accountability; DC context creates constant pressure toward cultural accommodation; large church culture can undermine deep community. For a man in DC wanting strong preaching and young adult community, Passion City DC is worth attending — evaluate the elder structure and men's ministry depth before committing long-term.

churches.assessment: Pillar Church of Stafford is part of the Praetorian Project — a NAMB-funded military-community church-planting network with direct leadership ties to McLean Bible Church's post-2016 church-planting infrastructure. Founding Pillar pastor Clint Clifton is the senior director of resource and research strategy at NAMB AND a Praetorian Project board member; Dale Sutherland (formerly McLean Bible) is listed as president of MBC's church-planting network. Strategically located near Quantico Marine Corps Base. PRIOR ASSESSMENT INCORRECTLY CHARACTERIZED THIS AS A STAFFORD BAPTIST PLANT — that was wrong; it is a Praetorian / NAMB / McLean-Bible-network plant. MOOP (Adam Johns) attended an event here and notes the McLean-Bible-network ties as a meaningful concern: McLean Bible has had significant post-2017 leadership controversy, multiple lawsuits, and post-2020 cultural turn. Adam's broader critique: "some church plants are just attempts to make a church look good on paper — they can't grow a church so they spread out." Pillar may be doing genuine military-community ministry, but the network parentage warrants visit-level discernment.

churches.assessment: Pinecrest ARP Church in Hendersonville, North Carolina (Flat Rock area) sits in the heart of ARP country — right near Bonclarken, the ARP denominational conference center. Senior Pastor Rhett Carson is from Gastonia, NC and Due West, SC (home of Erskine) — as ARP a pedigree as you can find. He holds degrees from Erskine College and Reformed Theological Seminary (Orlando) and served eight years in youth ministry before becoming senior pastor. Married to Kathy with five children. The church has a strong social media presence across Facebook, Instagram, YouTube, and Spotify. ARP male-only ordination and Westminster Standards align cleanly with the MOOP rubric. Green-rated orthodox Reformed option for the Asheville/Hendersonville area.

churches.assessment: Pohick Church is one of the oldest and most historically significant churches in Northern Virginia — originally built in 1774 and known as the parish of George Washington, George Mason, and other Virginia Founders. It is a landmark of American religious history. However, it remains affiliated with the Episcopal Church (TEC), which has undergone systematic theological abandonment since the 1970s — ordaining women as priests and bishops, affirming same-sex marriage, and ordaining LGBTQ+ clergy. The historic beauty of this church and its colonial American legacy are genuinely compelling, but the TEC institutional framework is doctrinally unreliable. Men seeking sound biblical preaching and complementarian theology should consider ACNA alternatives in Northern Virginia (such as The Falls Church Anglican or Truro Anglican), which left TEC precisely over these issues. churches.assessment: Portico Church is a Gospel-centered Southern Baptist congregation near downtown Charlottesville, pastored by Rev. Jason Conner under the BGAV (Baptist General Association of Virginia). The BGAV affiliation warrants mild caution — it is a state-level convention that can trend more moderate than the national SBC on cultural and gender issues. The church's own branding is 'Gospel Centered,' which is encouraging, and the Baptist Faith & Message 2000 provides a solid baseline for doctrine. Before committing, a man would want to attend in person, review sermon content, and ask directly about women in leadership and the church's stance on cultural issues. The orthodox foundation is likely solid; the BGAV context is the variable.

score_notes.christology: Heidelberg Catechism (Q&A 29–52) and Belgic Confession (Articles 18–21) confess orthodox Trinitarian and Chalcedonian Christology.
score_notes.scripture: Belgic Confession Articles 3–7 affirm the inspiration, sufficiency, and authority of canonical Scripture as the rule of faith.
score_notes.gender: RCUS Constitution restricts the offices of minister, elder, and deacon to qualified men only — male-only ordained officers.
score_notes.leadership: Plurality of male elders (consistory) under presbyterial-classical polity (classis and synod).
score_notes.soteriology: Three Forms of Unity — monergistic regeneration, sola fide, sola gratia, sola Scriptura, particular redemption per the Canons of Dort.
score_notes.cultural: RCUS / Eureka Classis fought a successful theological and legal battle to continue as the true RCUS when the parent body merged into the Evangelical and Reformed Church in 1934 — paradigmatic confessional resistance.
score_notes.denominational: Reformed Church in the United States — German Reformed heritage tracing to Boehm's 1725 organization in Pennsylvania; the modern RCUS preserves the Eureka Classis line.
score_notes.preaching: Catechetical preaching (Heidelberg Catechism Lord's Day series) is standard RCUS practice in the second service or Sunday school.
score_notes.mens_discipleship: Family worship, catechism instruction, and male headship in home and church are emphasized in the German Reformed tradition.
score_notes.mission: RCUS supports Westminster Biblical Missions and partners with NAPARC churches in domestic and foreign missions.

score_notes.preaching: Expository preaching standard in Reformed Baptist tradition.
score_notes.mens_discipleship: Reformed Baptist congregations typically maintain robust men's ministry / discipleship.
score_notes.mission: CBA member churches commonly partner with Founders Ministries and Reformed Baptist church-planting networks.

churches.name: Redeemer Bible Church
churches.overall_label: SBCV, complementarian, Pillar Network

score_notes.christology: Affirms the Baptist Faith & Message (2000), which holds to historic Trinitarian orthodoxy.
score_notes.scripture: The BFM 2000 affirms that the Bible is 'truth without any mixture of error'.
score_notes.gender: Male pastor Vic Carpenter confirmed; all listed staff leaders male (Jimmy Clanagan, Jakob Lyons, Bob Briggs, Glenn Prescott, Eric Wright). Complementarian practice observed.
score_notes.leadership: Vic Carpenter (Ph.D. SEBTS) + plural elders/staff; connected to sister church Redeemer Stafford.
score_notes.soteriology: Affirms the BFM 2000, which holds to salvation by grace through faith in Christ alone.
score_notes.cultural: No DEI/CRT or affirming language; inerrancy of Scripture preached as sermon topic.
score_notes.preaching: Sermon titles include 'Evidence for the Christian Faith,' 'Inerrancy of Scripture,' 'An Eschatological Position' — doctrinal/expository orientation confirmed.
score_notes.mission: Planted by Spotswood Baptist with a stated value of church planting.
score_notes.mens_discipleship: Dedicated /men/ ministry page confirmed on site.
score_notes.denominational: Pillar Network affiliation directly listed on church site under associations — confirms SBC-adjacent accountability. Pastor Vic Carpenter (Ph.D., SEBTS) confirmed. Elder page shows multiple male names (Clanagan, Lyons, Briggs, Prescott, Wright, et al.) — plurality of male elders confirmed.

churches.assessment: Redeemer Bible Church is a recent and highly promising church plant out of Spotswood Baptist. It is solidly grounded in conservative evangelical theology, formally affirming the Baptist Faith & Message (2000). The church is led by a well-educated pastor, Victor (Vic) Carpenter, who holds a Ph.D. from Southeastern Baptist Theological Seminary. Their leadership structure includes a plurality of male elders, and they have dedicated ministries for men, women, and children. For anyone seeking a complementarian, SBC-affiliated church with a high view of Scripture and a commitment to discipleship and church planting, Redeemer Bible Church is an excellent option in the Spotsylvania area. MOOP-context note (Adam Johns, 2026): Adam attended both Redeemer Bible Spotsy and Stafford and characterizes the network as "splants" from his home church Spotswood Baptist — the new chain catered to Spotswood members who were "more Calvinist leaning" than Spotswood's SBC mainstream. The Calvinist/Reformed Baptist leaning is theologically substantive (more rigorous soteriology) but the church-network history is partly a tactical accommodation rather than a pure missional plant. Worth understanding as inheritor of Spotswood's baseline orthodoxy + Reformed-Baptist refinement.
churches.gender_detail: BFM 2000 and all-male eldership confirm a complementarian stance.
churches.denomination_detail: SBC via SBCV; Pillar Network affiliation

churches.assessment: Redeemer Bible Church of Stafford is an excellent and promising new church plant, born out of Redeemer Bible Church in Spotsylvania. It upholds the same strong theological convictions, formally affirming the Baptist Faith & Message (2000). The church is governed by a biblical plurality of male elders and meets in an elementary school, typical of a new, growing congregation. For anyone in the Stafford area seeking a biblically solid, complementarian, SBC-affiliated church with a strong commitment to the Gospel, this is a top-tier recommendation. MOOP-context note (Adam Johns, 2026): Adam attended both Redeemer Bible churches and characterizes the network as "splants" from Spotswood Baptist via Redeemer Spotsy — a chain accommodating Spotswood members "more Calvinist leaning" than the SBC mainstream. Stafford is functionally a splant-of-a-splant (Spotswood → Redeemer Spotsy → Redeemer Stafford). Theologically substantive Reformed-Baptist refinement, but the network history is partly tactical accommodation rather than pure missional plant.

churches.assessment: Redeemer Church of Arlington is an Acts 29 church plant in Arlington, VA led by Marshall Griffin. Acts 29 is a respected church planting network founded by Mark Driscoll (now independent of him) focused on Gospel-centered, expository preaching and disciple-making. The church's stated mission — 'making disciples who follow Jesus into His Word, His world, and His family' — reflects a healthy integrative understanding of discipleship. Marshall Griffin was trained at Southeastern Baptist Theological Seminary, a conservative SBC school. For a man in the Arlington/DC metro area seeking a complementarian, Gospel-centered church with strong discipleship culture, Redeemer Arlington is a solid recommendation. Verify current elder board and ministry culture directly.

It is affiliated with the SBC of Virginia, grounding it in the Southern Baptist Convention's confessional framework (Baptist Faith & Message 2000). Justin Pearson planted and pastored Sojourn Fairfax through the Acts 29 and Sojourn Network. The merger created a stronger combined congregation in Fairfax County. SBC affiliation provides meaningful confessional accountability — BF&M 2000 affirms biblical inerrancy, complementarian gender theology, and exclusive salvation through Jesus Christ. For a man in the Fairfax/Burke/Springfield area wanting a SBC-affiliated, Gospel-centered church with solid preaching and discipleship culture, RGC Fairfax is a solid recommendation. Verify current elder structure and men's ministry programs directly.

score_notes.christology: Redemption Church exists to exalt Christ, equip the saints, and engage the lost, for the glory of God.
score_notes.scripture: We believe that God gives life through His Word, and so we are committed to preaching consecutively through books of the Bible while pointing to Christ from all of Scripture.
score_notes.soteriology: In Him we have redemption through His blood, the forgiveness of our trespasses, according to the riches of His grace...
score_notes.gender: Deacons are men and women who meet the biblical qualifications given in 1 Timothy 3:8-13.
score_notes.leadership: It is the biblical conviction of Redemption Church that the New Testament presents the church being led by a plurality of pastors/elders.
score_notes.preaching: Christ-centered Expositional Preaching We believe that God gives life through His Word, and so we are committed to preaching consecutively through books of the Bible while pointing to Christ from all of Scripture.
score_notes.mission: We believe in the centrality of the local church in fulfilling the Great Commission, and so we are committed to engaging the lost both at home and abroad through the raising up and sending out of qualified Gospel-workers to start and strengthen churches.
score_notes.cultural: We believe that following Jesus is full of both joy and sacrifice, and so we are committed to calling each other to lives of repentance and holiness by saying no to our own sin and the sinful things of this world.

churches.assessment: Reformation Bible Church in Melbourne, FL is a Reformed Baptist, father-led, family-integrated congregation committed to the sufficiency of Scripture and the glory of God. Their motto — 'By the Gospel and for King Jesus… We Build. We Fight. We Conquer' — signals a militant, Christendom-oriented posture that aligns with the Right Response Ministries vision. The father-led structure is explicitly patriarchal (GREEN on gender — not merely complementarian). Family integrated services with potluck fellowship suggest a tight-knit covenant community. Friend Michael Pflugrad is connected through the Right Response Ministries Christendom cohort of 2025. This is the kind of church the MOOP directory was built to highlight.

churches.name: Refuge Church
churches.pastor: Pastor Brian Sauvé (Lead), Eric Conn, Dan Berkholder, Kevin Giffin, Ben Garrett (Elder Plurality)
churches.pastor_credentials: Brian Sauvé — author, musician, Reformed theologian
churches.overall_label: Strong Theological Alignment

score_notes.christology: Reformed confessional tradition affirms the full deity and humanity of Christ — Nicene orthodoxy. Green.
score_notes.scripture: Reformed tradition holds to the inerrancy and supreme authority of Scripture. Green.
score_notes.gender: Brian Sauvé is a nationally known voice for biblical complementarianism and patriarchal household vision. Male-only pastors/elders. Quiverfull-adjacent emphasis on family formation.
score_notes.leadership: R44 refetch confirms direct quote: 'a plurality of qualified pastor/elders' governs the church. Elder plurality structure verified on site. Green stands.
score_notes.soteriology: Reformed theology — salvation by grace alone through faith alone, doctrines of grace affirmed.
score_notes.cultural: Explicitly counter-cultural. Refuge has faced criticism for strong traditional Christian stances on masculinity, family formation, and women's roles — but these align with biblical teaching.
score_notes.preaching: Reformed church with expository tradition; Brian Sauvé is a writer and preacher committed to verse-by-verse teaching.
score_notes.mission: Church planted in Ogden, Utah — one of the most spiritually challenging mission fields in the US (heavy LDS culture). Commendable gospel presence.
score_notes.mens_discipleship: Strong men's formation culture. Brian Sauvé writes and teaches extensively on biblical masculinity.
score_notes.denominational: Independent. No formal denominational accountability is a minor concern, but elder plurality structure provides internal checks.

churches.assessment: Refuge Church in Ogden, Utah is a Reformed congregation led by pastor Brian Sauvé — a nationally known author and teacher on biblical masculinity, patriarchal households, and Reformed theology. The church holds strong complementarian convictions and preaches expository, confessional Christianity in the heart of LDS-dominated Utah. Critics on Reddit have called it 'cult-like' for its emphasis on large families and women's roles — standard internet blowback against any church that takes the Bible seriously on gender. The 'Mark and Avoid' site flag (from April 2025) regarding Eric Conn should be investigated. The theological foundation is solid. For men in the Ogden area looking for a doctrinally serious, biblically masculine church culture in a difficult mission field — Refuge is one of the strongest options in the region. Verify current leadership stability before committing.
churches.gender_detail: Male-only elders and pastors. Strong complementarian household vision. Brian Sauvé is a leading voice on biblical manhood.
churches.denomination_detail: Independent Reformed — no formal denominational affiliation

Pastor Jason Nix came on as Lead Pastor in May 2023 with 15+ years of ministry experience. The congregation currently gathers at the Arlington Music Hall while establishing itself. As a brand-new GMC plant rather than a transitioned former UMC congregation, this church's identity is defined entirely by orthodox Wesleyan doctrine from inception — no legacy progressivism to unwind. score_notes.scripture: Verbal plenary inspiration: "the Holy Scriptures are the very Word of God, verbally inspired in all parts and therefore wholly without mixture of error as originally revealed." Adopts BF&M 2000 verbatim. Inerrancy explicit.
score_notes.gender: Male-only elders/pastors confirmed via leadership page (all three Staff Elders are men; only role given to a woman is Minister to Children and Director of Nursery Ministry, consistent with complementarian SBC norm). BF&M 2000 adoption locks in complementarian pastoral office.
score_notes.leadership: Polity explicitly stated: 'We are ruled by Jesus, led by the Elders, and governed by the congregation.' Plurality of male elders (Dorsey, Bench, Milton) with congregational accountability — the textbook elder-led congregational pattern advocated by 9Marks. Pastor answerable to the elder team and to the congregation.
score_notes.soteriology: Reformed-Baptist soteriology in the doctrinal essentials: total depravity ('man... has become separated from, and spiritually dead to God through Adam’s sin... possessing depraved human nature with no spark of divine life'), monergistic grace ('salvation is a free and permanent gift of God that cannot be secured or merited in part or in whole by any virtue or good work of man'), substitutionary atonement, perseverance ('salvation is inextricably bound to righteous living and good works and is the inevitable consequence (not the procuring cause) of the new life implanted by the Holy Spirit'). Faith alone explicit.
score_notes.cultural: No DEI/CRT or progressive-justice framing found anywhere on site. SBTC affiliation is the conservative Texas convention (split from BGCT in 1998 over inerrancy and trajectory). Stated mission language is gospel-centered ('herald... gracious proclamation of the Gospel').
score_notes.preaching: 'Our normal method of teaching is a verse-by-verse study of a book of the Bible.' Expository confirmed. Sermon archive shows 6,321 messages across 58+ series including book studies of John, Galatians, Colossians, Ephesians, Habakkuk, Esther, Philemon, 1 Timothy, Hebrews, Psalms, and Sermon on the Mount — systematic exposition over years.
score_notes.mission: Strong outward focus: 'Grow. Serve. Go.' core. Local missions arm 'For the City' (launched 2017) plus adopted missionaries (Adopted Missions Request form). Hispanic plant in 1981. Great Commission framed as primary purpose statement.
score_notes.mens_discipleship: Dedicated 'RidgeMen Ministry' — explicit goal: 'equip men to build Christ-centered relationships through Bible study, service, leadership, and community.' Led by Joel Bench (Pastor of Discipleship). Independent men's page and contact path confirmed.
score_notes.denominational: Dual-aligned SBC + SBTC. SBTC is the conservative-inerrantist alternative to BGCT. Elder plurality plus congregational governance plus dual denominational accountability is among the tightest accountability structures available in SBC life.

churches.assessment: Ridgecrest Baptist Church in Greenville is exactly the kind of church the directory wants to surface: 60-year-old (founded 1965) conservative SBC congregation, dual-aligned with the Southern Baptists of Texas Convention (the conservative split from BGCT, not the BGCT itself), explicitly adopting Baptist Faith & Message 2000, led by a plurality of male Staff Elders (Nick Dorsey, Joel Bench, Justin Milton) under the polity statement 'ruled by Jesus, led by the Elders, governed by the congregation' — the 9Marks elder-led-congregational pattern. The 'reformed-ish' descriptor the submitter used is well-earned: the doctrinal essentials affirm total depravity, monergistic grace, substitutionary atonement, and perseverance, even though the church does not formally subscribe to the 1689 London Baptist Confession or claim a Founders Ministry affiliation on its public site. Preaching is explicitly verse-by-verse expository, with a sermon archive of 6,321 messages spanning systematic book studies (John, Galatians, Colossians, Ephesians, Habakkuk, Esther, Philemon, 1 Timothy, Hebrews, Psalms, Sermon on the Mount). The 'RidgeMen' men's ministry is dedicated and pastor-led. The local missions arm 'For the City' (launched 2017) and a Spanish-language plant from 1981 demonstrate Great Commission seriousness. Past pastoral roster (Pratt, McGinlay, Hamilton, Stubblefield, Douglass, Herbert, Beasley, now Dorsey) shows stable conservative trajectory. No drift signals, no female pastoral roles above women's ministry, no progressive-justice language. Submitter Ben Collins's characterization — 'fairly conventionally conservative SBC church, led by a reformed-ish pastor with outstanding shepherding and preaching skills... a great opportunity for a strong male community' — is independently corroborated by the church's own published material. Solid GREEN, no qualifiers.

score_notes.christology: Beliefs page explicitly affirms triune God with 'distinct personal attributes'; Christ as 'fully God, fully man' and 'the eternal Son of God'; exclusivity stated: 'There is no salvation apart from personal faith in Jesus Christ as Lord.' Full Nicene orthodoxy via BF&M 2000.
score_notes.scripture: BF&M 2000 inerrancy adopted verbatim: 'All Scripture is totally true and trustworthy...truth, without any mixture of error.' Authority over creeds and opinions affirmed.
score_notes.gender: BF&M 2000 complementarian framework: 'the office of pastor is limited to men as qualified by Scripture'; marriage 'uniting of one man and one woman'; husband headship / wife submission modeled on Christ-church. Explicit opposition to 'all forms of sexual immorality, including adultery, homosexuality, and pornography.' All three lead pastors and all four lay Church Council members are male.
score_notes.leadership: Self-described as 'Council-Led, Congregational.' Church Council functions as elders/overseers/pastors and includes three male lead pastors + four elected male lay members (Chad White, Dave Velloney, Jeff Benson, Rusty Bailey). Plural-elder model with congregational accountability on budgets, officer elections, constitutional amendments, and pastoral staff calls. Strong polity.
score_notes.soteriology: BF&M 2000 sola fide: 'Salvation involves the redemption of the whole man, and is offered freely to all who accept Jesus Christ as Lord and Saviour'; baptism explicitly symbolic, not salvific (Section VII). Regeneration / justification / sanctification / glorification model articulated.
score_notes.cultural: No DEI/CRT framing found on Our Beliefs, leadership, or homepage. Traditional sexual ethics maintained throughout. Vision statement is Christocentric: 'Living every day captivated and changed by Jesus.'
score_notes.preaching: Sermon archive evidences expository book-by-book preaching — current series include 'Unfinished Work: Titus' and 'The Last Week' (Mark). All three lead pastors rotate as primary preachers.
score_notes.mission: Four-pillar strategy: Worship, Connect, Serve, Go (missions & outreach). Executive Director of Missions and Outreach is a senior staff role. Great Commission framing throughout.
score_notes.mens_discipleship: Dedicated Men's Ministry page in primary navigation. Programs include Men's Groups (via Church Center) and 'ManCake' men's breakfast. Stated emphasis on 'the biblical leadership role of men in the home and in the Body of Christ' with Proverbs 27:17 iron-sharpens-iron framing.
score_notes.denominational: Southern Baptist Convention via explicit BF&M 2000 adoption. Planted out of South Norfolk Baptist Church (purchased the 11.5-acre Great Bridge Blvd property in 1998 and sent the church plant). SBC accountability + Baptist heritage.

churches.assessment: River Oak Church is a strong SBC option for Hampton Roads-area men. The church plants out of South Norfolk Baptist Church (1998 land purchase, 1999 first service at Oscar F. Smith High School, 2000 formal constitution, 2007 facility opening on Great Bridge Blvd), and adopts the Baptist Faith and Message 2000 verbatim. The doctrinal statement hits every conservative-evangelical mark: triune God, full deity and exclusivity of Christ, inerrant Scripture as 'totally true and trustworthy...without any mixture of error,' salvation by grace through faith alone, believer's baptism by immersion, complementarian marriage and pastoral office ('the office of pastor is limited to men'), and explicit opposition to homosexuality and sexual immorality. Governance is 'Council-Led, Congregational' — a hybrid plural-elder + congregational-vote model where the three Co-Lead Pastors (Hammen, Waldrop, LaRussa, all called 2024) plus four elected male lay councilors function as elders/overseers/pastors and the congregation votes on budgets, officer elections, constitutional amendments, and pastoral calls. Preaching is expository (current series through Titus and Mark). Dedicated Men's Ministry with Men's Groups and the ManCake breakfast confirms intentional men's discipleship. No DEI/CRT or affirming language found on the public pages. Green across all ten dimensions.

churches.assessment: River of Grace Lutheran Church is affiliated with the ELCA (Evangelical Lutheran Church in America), the largest but most theologically liberal Lutheran denomination in North America. In 2009 the ELCA voted to ordain practicing homosexuals and allow blessing of same-sex unions — a clear departure from biblical sexuality (Romans 1, 1 Corinthians 6). The ELCA also rejects biblical inerrancy and has absorbed progressive social justice theology. Individual congregations may have faithful pastors who preach soundly despite the denomination, but the institutional framework provides no protection and active opposition to biblical sexuality. For a man wanting a doctrinally sound church with biblical authority and complementarian gender theology, an ELCA church is not recommended without careful individual investigation. Consider Missouri Synod or Wisconsin Synod Lutheran alternatives in the area.

Founded 1992 by Chris and Miriam Phillips after four years as missionaries in Brazil; the congregation began as Living Water Fellowship in a Henderson Drive storefront and was renamed River of Life Church.
