churches.assessment: Rivermont Evangelical Presbyterian Church is one of Lynchburg's most theologically distinguished congregations. Founded in 1881 — over 140 years of ministry in the same Lynchburg neighborhood — Rivermont operates under the Westminster Confession of Faith and Catechisms within the EPC (Evangelical Presbyterian Church). Dr. David Weber's preaching is highly regarded by long-time members. The church's membership in the New River Presbytery provides genuine external accountability, confessional standards, and doctrinal oversight absent in independent churches. For a man wanting Reformed theology, historic confessional Christianity, and a church with deep Lynchburg roots and community presence, Rivermont EPC is a top-tier choice. The Campus Outreach ministry on staff signals a heart for the next generation.

churches.assessment: Riverside Church at Park & King is a Florida-historical case of SBC departure over both LGBTQ+ affirmation and (subsequently) female pastoral leadership. The church separated from the Southern Baptist Convention in 2009 after then-FL Baptist Convention Executive Director John Sullivan challenged the church's LGBTQ+ acceptance; today the church is openly affirming, lists female pastoral leadership (Pastor Courtney, Rev. Clair), and is a member of the Association of Welcoming and Affirming Baptists, the Alliance of Baptists, and the Cooperative Baptist Fellowship. Pre-2020 departure date noted; included as a FL SBC drift datapoint because it remains widely cross-listed in legacy SBC directories and demonstrates the FL Baptist Convention's enforcement pattern that later led to the 2023 Freedom Church and 2026 Crossing Church disfellowshipments.

churches.assessment: Rock Church International is one of Hampton Roads' most historic megachurches — founded in 1968 by Bishops John and Anne Gimenez as a Pentecostal congregation with national impact. The church hosted major Washington For Jesus rallies in the 1980s and 1990s drawing hundreds of thousands to DC. Today, Senior Pastors John and Robin Blanchard lead the congregation. The primary concern for complementarian men: Robin Blanchard serves as a co-Senior Pastor, and the church's history includes female episcopal leadership (Bishop Anne Gimenez). For men committed to biblical male-only eldership/pastoral leadership, this is a disqualifying red flag. The church's charismatic heritage and Pentecostal theology require evaluation for those outside that tradition. Rock Church has genuine gospel impact and community roots, but the gender/leadership structure places it outside clear biblical complementarianism.

churches.overall_label: Confessionally Reformed — RPCNA (Westminster + exclusive psalmody)
churches.services: Sunday School 10:00 AM; Morning Worship 11:00 AM; Evening Worship 6:30 PM; Midweek Bible Study 7:00 PM (1st/3rd/5th Wed)

score_notes.christology: Westminster Standards — Trinitarian, Chalcedonian Christology fully affirmed.
score_notes.scripture: Westminster Confession of Faith Ch. 1 — Scripture inerrant and the only infallible rule of faith and practice.
score_notes.gender: RPCNA restricts offices of elder, deacon, and minister to qualified men; strong patriarchal household tradition.
score_notes.leadership: Plurality of male elders + RPCNA Constitution accountability via Presbytery and Synod.
score_notes.soteriology: Westminster soteriology — sovereign grace, monergism, sola fide, definite atonement.
score_notes.cultural: RPCNA Testimony (Reformed Presbyterian Testimony) explicitly addresses cultural issues; Covenanter heritage of cultural distinctiveness.
score_notes.denominational: RPCNA — historic Covenanter Presbyterian body, Westminster Standards + RP Testimony, exclusive psalmody and a cappella worship.
score_notes.preaching: Expository Christ-centered preaching of the whole counsel of God per Westminster standards.
score_notes.mens_discipleship: Strong Covenanter heritage of male spiritual leadership; men's prayer fellowship common.
score_notes.mission: RPCNA engages home missions (church planting) and global missions (Japan, Cyprus, South Sudan, etc.).

The congregation is fully LGBTQIA+ welcoming and affirming, was previously declared out of fellowship with the Dallas Baptist Association over ordaining a practicing-homosexual deacon, and aligns with CBF and the Alliance of Baptists. churches.assessment: Saddleback Church is one of the most influential churches in American history through Rick Warren's 'Purpose Driven' model. However, the church made the fateful decision to ordain women as pastors, leading to their disfellowship from the Southern Baptist Convention in 2023. This is not a minor issue — it represents a direct rejection of complementarian biblical interpretation. Warren's 'Purpose Driven' model also substitutes topical/practical preaching for expository teaching. Under Andy Wood, the church has continued on this egalitarian trajectory. RED — the ordination of women pastors is a deal-breaker on MOOP's rubric.

Clark is a Mathews, VA native who planted Salt Church in 2021 starting from a living room. The church meets Sundays at 10:02 AM at the Hartfield YMCA. score_notes.christology: Jesus Christ is the Son of God. He is co-equal with the Father. Jesus was both fully God and fully human, lived a sinless human life, and offered himself as a perfect sacrifice for the sins of all people by dying on a cross.
score_notes.scripture: The Bible is God’s Word to us. It was written by human authors under the supernatural guidance of the Holy Spirit. It is the supreme source of truth for Christian beliefs and living. Because it is inspired by God, it is truth without mixture of error.

churches.assessment: Second Baptist Church (West End) is a historically important Richmond Black congregation with roots stretching over 185 years. Rev. Dr. James Henry Harris is a serious scholar — Distinguished Professor of Homiletics at Virginia Union University and a published theologian. The problem: Rev. Harris is an academic whose theological framework is aligned with Black liberation theology, a school of thought that subordinates Scripture to the experience of racial oppression and reinterprets the Gospel through social and political liberation categories. This is not a Reformed or evangelical framework — it places experience and culture above Scripture's authority. For men seeking a doctrinally sound, Great Commission-focused church, Second Baptist (West End) is not the right fit. The historical legacy is real and deserves respect; the current theological direction is not.

churches.assessment: Selah is a young, Spirit-filled church led by genuinely gospel-loving people. Luke Taylor is a sincere pastor with solid theology on the essentials — Christ is the only way, the Bible is authoritative, gender is binary. But structural concerns are real: no elder accountability, women functioning in pastoral roles, and a spiritual formation emphasis that can trend contemplative rather than expository. If you're a man who needs clear authority structures and complementarian conviction, visit with your eyes open. If you're a new believer or seeking family, you'll find genuine love here. Just ask the hard questions early.

churches.assessment: Shiloh Baptist Church (New Site) and Shiloh Baptist (Old Site) are sister congregations sharing common roots stretching back to the pre-Civil War African Baptist Church of Fredericksburg. Where Old Site (801 Sophia St) has drifted toward social-gospel framing, New Site presents a cleaner mission statement: 'Glorifying God, making disciples, and serving humanity' — with 'making disciples' as the explicit Great Commission anchor. Rev. Keenan Thomas arrived in October 2022 with a Howard University / Drew Seminary education and a practical ministry background at Alfred Street Baptist (one of the largest and most Word-focused Black Baptist churches in the country). His foundational scripture — 1 Peter 4:11, speaking 'the very words of God' — reflects a high view of Scripture in praxis. The honest concern is Drew Theological Seminary, which is a theologically progressive Methodist institution — not the formation environment that produces expository complementarians. However, a man's seminary doesn't always define his ministry convictions. The 15+ ministries and Wednesday Bible study suggest an active, Word-engaged congregation. Worth visiting and hearing Rev. Keenan preach before drawing conclusions.

churches.assessment: Shiloh Baptist Church (Old Site) is one of Fredericksburg's most historically significant congregations — founded in 1854 from a congregation dating to the early 1800s, serving the African American community through slavery, the Civil War, Reconstruction, and the Civil Rights era. Notable members include John Washington (whose escape from slavery inspired a Trail to Freedom) and Rev. Lawrence A. Davies (pastor and mayor of Fredericksburg). The church's commitment to community (free Wednesday breakfast with Micah Ecumenical Ministries, active youth ministry) reflects genuine love. The honest theological concern is the public framing: 'no barriers to God's grace, no walls of exclusion' and 'inclusive embrace' language combined with minimal gospel-clarity and strong social-service identity suggests the congregation may have drifted toward social gospel territory where the transforming work of Christ is framed primarily in terms of social healing rather than personal salvation and sanctification. This is a pattern in mainline-influenced progressive Baptist churches. Moop should visit and listen to the sermons directly before drawing conclusions.

Theologically, the parish holds the historic Catholic positions: Nicene-Chalcedonian Christology, male-only priesthood, traditional sexual ethics, opposition to abortion. Within the Roman Catholic tradition, Blessed Sacrament is unremarkable in its orthodoxy and is a serious, traditional Catholic parish.

churches.worship_distinctive: Exclusive psalmody (sings only the biblical Psalms in worship) and a cappella worship (no musical instruments). This is the distinctive RPCNA Covenanter worship pattern — rooted in the regulative principle of worship and unbroken since the Scottish Covenanter tradition. Twice-Sunday Lord's Day services are standard.
churches.assessment: Sparta RPC is a historic Covenanter congregation in Southern Illinois — Sparta has been an RPCNA outpost since the 19th century, when Covenanter Scots-Irish settlers planted churches across the rural Midwest. Holds Westminster Confession with strict confessional subscription, practices exclusive psalmody and a cappella worship (no instruments), maintains twice-Sunday services. Male-only ordination, deeply complementarian, no cultural drift. The exclusive psalmody and a cappella worship will be a major adjustment for those not raised in this tradition, but Sparta represents one of the oldest unbroken confessional Reformed witnesses in the rural Midwest. Illinois has very few RPCNA congregations; Sparta is a meaningful historic anchor.

churches.assessment: Sen. Edmund S. Muskie (D-ME) — U.S. Senator 1959-1980, Governor of Maine 1955-1959 (the state's first Roman Catholic governor), Secretary of State 1980-1981 under President Carter, and 1968 Democratic vice-presidential nominee — was born March 28, 1914 in Rumford, Maine to Polish immigrant parents Stephen Marciszewski (anglicized to Muskie 1914) and Josephine née Czarnecka. Muskie's first language was Polish; he spoke only Polish until age 4. St. Athanasius Church — established 1895 on Maine Avenue, sanctuary rebuilt 1928 — was the primary Roman Catholic parish serving Rumford's Polish and Eastern European immigrant Catholic community during Muskie's childhood. While Wikipedia's Muskie biography directly confirms his Roman Catholic identity ("the state's first Roman Catholic governor") and his Polish-Rumford upbringing without explicitly naming the parish, St. Athanasius's historic role as the Rumford Polish Catholic parish makes it the logical family parish; the Franco American Digital Archives Edmund S. Muskie Oral History Collection contains an interview specifically referencing St. Athanasius and St. John Parish Rumford in connection with Muskie. JD Vance was baptized and confirmed here in August 2019. The Dominican priest who guided his conversion, Fr. Henry Stephan, OP, met with Vance for months over coffee and lunch discussing theology, mysticism, and moral philosophy. churches.assessment: St. James' Episcopal Church in Hyde Park was Franklin D. Roosevelt's lifelong parish — he served on the vestry and as senior warden, even continuing in that role during his presidency. He, Eleanor, and the Roosevelt family worshiped here whenever they were at the Hyde Park estate (now the Home of FDR National Historic Site, 2.7 miles south of the church). Founded 1811 by residents including Samuel Bard (George Washington's physician), it remains an active parish of the Episcopal Diocese of New York under recently installed Rector The Rev. Meredith Kadet Sanderson (October 2025). The church is theologically within TEC's mainline trajectory — orthodox in creedal Christology, but progressive on sexuality and ordination per General Convention decisions. Beautiful Hudson Valley historic site; significant theological distance from MOOP's confessional commitments.

churches.assessment: St. Joseph's on Capitol Hill is a Roman Catholic parish in the Archdiocese of Washington at 313 2nd Street NE — less than half a mile from the Capitol and Supreme Court buildings. Known as "the Senate church" because of its proximity to the Senate side of the Capitol (the House-side counterpart is St. Peter's on Capitol Hill). Its location has long attracted members of Congress, congressional staffers, and Supreme Court justices to daily Mass — historical attendees documented include Senators John E. Kenna, Robert F. Kennedy, Ted Kennedy, and Justice Antonin Scalia. Current pastor Rev. William H. Gurnee III. Founded 1868. Per MOOP Protestant frame this is YELLOW — Catholic sacramental soteriology and Magisterium-Scripture-Tradition triad fall outside sola fide / sola scriptura, but the parish carries no particular doctrinal anomalies within Catholic standards. Included for situational awareness about a key DC Catholic parish serving the legislative + judicial branches.

churches.assessment: St. Jude's Anglican Church is an REC/ACNA congregation in Richmond — and the Reformed Episcopal Church is one of the most doctrinally rigorous Anglican bodies in existence. Founded in 1873 as a protest against Catholic ritualism in the Anglican tradition, the REC holds to Protestant soteriology (justification by faith alone), Reformation Anglican standards (39 Articles, Book of Common Prayer), male-only clergy, and traditional biblical ethics. Very Rev. W. Scott Thompson leads a congregation described as 'a traditional congregation focused on Jesus Christ, His Gospel, and worship through Word and Sacrament.' This is exactly the kind of clarity men committed to Reformed orthodoxy need: no ambiguity on gender, no denominational drift, no social justice crowding out the Gospel. The REC/ACNA dual affiliation means accountability in both the richest Reformed Anglican tradition and the broader ACNA network. One of the strongest options for any man who loves liturgy, Reformed soteriology, and biblical authority.

churches.assessment: St. Martin's Episcopal Church in Houston is the largest Episcopal congregation in the United States by membership and attendance. The Bush family — George H.W. and Barbara Bush — joined St. Martin's after moving from Midland in 1959, raised their five children there (including future president George W. Bush), and returned in 1993 upon leaving the White House. President George H.W. Bush's 2018 funeral was held at St. Martin's. Rev. Russell Levenson Jr. served as rector 2007-2024, and Rev. Dane Boston (formerly Dean of Trinity Episcopal Cathedral, Columbia SC) was installed in 2025. Institutionally TEC has fully departed from biblical authority on sexual ethics since 2003, ordains women as bishops since 1989, and performs same-sex marriages. St. Martin's under Levenson positioned itself as the more traditional mediating wing of TEC, but remained in TEC rather than departing to ACNA. Per MOOP rubric this is RED at the denominational level; included for situational awareness about the Bush family church.

churches.assessment: Saint Mary's is a large, active Catholic parish in Fredericksburg under the conservative Diocese of Arlington. Fr. Mosimann serves as Vicar Forane — essentially the area dean — indicating a significant, well-resourced congregation. Trinitarian orthodoxy is rock-solid; male-only priesthood is firmly complementarian; accountability structure is hierarchical and thorough. From a Protestant evangelical standpoint, the theological divergence is real: Catholic soteriology adds sacraments, merit, and ecclesial mediation to faith; Scripture sits alongside Tradition rather than above it. These are not minor differences — they were the substance of the Reformation. That said, for a man interested in robust liturgy, deep historical tradition, strong pro-life stance, and conservative moral theology, the Diocese of Arlington Catholic experience is among the best available. Not the right fit for a faith-alone evangelical, but should be evaluated on its own terms.

churches.assessment: Rep. Daniel D. Rostenkowski (D-IL), Chairman of the House Ways and Means Committee 1981-1994, was a son of the Polish-Catholic Chicago community served by St. Stanislaus Kostka — the "mother church" of Chicago's Polish parishes (1867), administered by the Resurrectionist Order since 1869. The Kennedy Expressway's famous "Rostenkowski Curve" exists because Rostenkowski intervened legislatively to alter the highway path and prevent demolition of St. Stanislaus Kostka. The parish remains an active Archdiocese of Chicago Polish-cathedral-style landmark and Sanctuary of Divine Mercy. Catholic parishes are scored Yellow as standing outside the Protestant confessional frame MOOP uses.

churches.assessment: Stony Point Reformed Presbyterian is an RPCNA congregation — one of the most theologically conservative Reformed denominations in North America. The RPCNA holds exclusively to the Westminster Standards, practices exclusive psalmody (singing only Psalms in worship without musical instruments), and maintains strict confessional subscription. This is the gold standard for confessional Reformed orthodoxy. The exclusive psalmody and a cappella worship will not suit everyone, but for those seeking the most confessionally rigorous Reformed option in Richmond, this is it. Strong complementarian leadership, inerrancy, and covenant theology.
churches.gender_detail: RPCNA strictly complementarian — male-only elders and deacons

churches.assessment: Strong Tower Church has a compelling outward presentation — three Sunday services, a "vibrant and diverse" congregation, and Lead Pastor Jeffrey Smith who is articulate, community-engaged, and served as invocation chaplain for the American Veterans Ball. However, two red flags emerge upon investigation: (1) Nicola Smith is listed as Associate Pastor — a female in a pastoral office, which stands outside complementarian biblical standards for church leadership. (2) Jeffrey Smith serves as Director of Cornerstone Global Network under Bishop Michael Pitts, a charismatic apostolic network model that can blur the lines between Scripture authority and apostolic/prophetic authority. For a man with strong complementarian convictions and a high view of Scripture as the final authority, these are not minor concerns. Not recommended without major doctrinal clarification.

churches.assessment: Sugar Creek Baptist Church is a large multi-campus SBC church in the Houston metro area led by Dr. Mark Hartman since 2002. Doctrinally, the church affirms Trinitarian theology, the Bible as 'true and fully accurate,' and salvation as a free gift through faith in Christ — all solid positions. The church appears complementarian in practice (pastoral titles for men, support roles for women) though not explicitly stated. Three campuses with multiple service styles including traditional, contemporary, and Spanish-language. Major concern: no dedicated men's ministry despite being a large church with 100+ staff. The church emphasizes community through Connect Groups and has strong mission language. SBC affiliation provides denominational accountability. Needs in-person evaluation to verify preaching style and cultural alignment.

Women serve as Women's Ministry Associates, Children's Minister, Preschool Ministry Director, Children's Elementary Director, Director of Pastoral Care. churches.assessment: The Falls Church Anglican has one of the most remarkable stories in American Christianity. As one of America's oldest churches (1734), it separated from The Episcopal Church over homosexuality and women's ordination, fought a legal battle that cost them their historic building, and re-planted as a faithful Anglican congregation. They now worship at an office building — having chosen doctrinal integrity over real estate. Rector Sam Ferguson leads a congregation with deep roots in biblical Anglicanism, liturgical worship rooted in Scripture, and a legacy of sending. ACNA accountability, male-only priesthood, complementarian household vision. For a man who values covenantal worship, historic liturgy, and a congregation that has paid a price for orthodoxy — this is worth serious consideration.
churches.gender_detail: Male Rector Sam Ferguson; DOMA permits women priests. Specific Falls Church policy not stated on fetched content.
churches.denomination_detail: ACNA — Diocese of the Mid-Atlantic (DOMA); Jerusalem Declaration, 39 Articles, BCP

churches.name: The Moody Church
churches.pastor: Dr. Philip Miller (17th Senior Pastor, appointed 2020)
churches.overall_label: Historic Moody — inerrancy, Trinity, complementarian

score_notes.christology: Doctrinal statement: 'exists eternally in a loving tri-unity (trinity) of three equally divine Persons: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit.' Orthodox Trinitarian.
score_notes.scripture: 'The Bible is without error in the original writings, the complete revelation of His will' — explicit inerrancy.
score_notes.gender: Distinct roles for deacons and deaconesses; male elder/pastor office implied but not quoted with headship framing — complementarian.
score_notes.leadership: Document references 'the Elders' as governing body — plurality of male elders.
score_notes.soteriology: 'Shed His blood on the cross as the perfect, all-sufficient sacrifice for our sins' — explicit penal substitution.
score_notes.cultural: No DEI/CRT language; traditional sexual ethics implied through Genesis creation framing.
score_notes.preaching: Preaching methodology not detailed on beliefs page; Moody tradition is expository but not confirmed from fetched content.
score_notes.mission: Moody historic evangelistic foundation; Great Commission orientation presumed but specific mission statement not quoted.
score_notes.mens_discipleship: Not addressed on fetched page; existing record flags men's ministry true — verify.
score_notes.denominational: Independent non-denominational; D. L. Moody historic legacy. Formal elder board with 10 named male elders (Jonathan Hauser Chairman, Joseph Carré Vice-Chairman, Kevin Baloue, Maximo Bermudez, Tony Durns, Stephen Farish, Steve Giere, Berv Peterson, Tom Sawyer, Phil Zahn) + Senior Pastor Philip Miller + Executive Pastor Bertsche + Pastor Emeritus Lutzer. Explicit inerrancy doctrinal statement and 17-pastor succession history establish verifiable governance. No formal confessional body membership. YELLOW under refined rubric (strong elder plurality + governance + heritage, no named network).

churches.assessment: The Moody Church is one of the most historically significant evangelical churches in America, rooted in the legacy of D.L. Moody. Dr. Erwin Lutzer served as the 16th pastor for 36 years (1980-2016), establishing it as a bastion of conservative evangelical theology. Dr. Philip Miller became the 17th Senior Pastor in 2020. The church is at the intersection of North Ave, Clark St, and LaSalle St in Chicago. Deep commitment to biblical authority, missions, and expository preaching. A historic evangelical landmark.
churches.gender_detail: Complementarian structure via deacons/deaconesses and male-only elder office (implied); specific pastor roster not on fetched page.
churches.denomination_detail: Non-denominational; historic tie to D. L. Moody (founded 1864)
churches.enrichment_notes: Strong, explicit doctrinal statement on inerrancy, Trinity, and substitutionary atonement. Independence keeps denominational dim at red.

score_notes.mens_discipleship: No dedicated men's discipleship program found for Fredericksburg campus. | RED: MOOP-personal-attendance report (Adam Johns, 2026-04): "I couldn't stay with the Mount — they weren't interested in really having a men's ministry, it seemed to me." Adam attended both Fredericksburg and Stafford campuses across multiple visits. Lack of men's discipleship interest is a core MOOP rubric concern (one of the 6 GREEN-required categories).
score_notes.denominational: Multi-site BGAV congregation (formerly Mount Ararat Baptist Church, est. 1907). BGAV publicly differentiated itself from the Southern Baptist Convention in November 2023 over women in pastoral roles, and the BGAV framework permits women pastors. The Fredericksburg campus's own pastoral team is currently male, but the denominational framework and multi-site streaming model keep this campus on the cautious side of yellow at the denominational dimension.

score_notes.scripture: Baptist biblical authority; BGAV churches typically affirm high view of Scripture though inerrancy not universally required.
score_notes.soteriology: Baptist sola fide tradition standard within BGAV range.
score_notes.mission: 'Multiplying disciples of Jesus' and 'church for ONE MORE' vision — explicit Great Commission framing.

churches.assessment: The Mount Fredericksburg has a campus pastor, Andrew Brothers, with a solid missions background and genuine evangelistic heart. The 'church For One More' vision is outreach-forward in a healthy way, and the Baptist DNA keeps the basics in place. Two key concerns: (1) BGAV affiliation places them in the moderate Virginia Baptist stream rather than SBC — BGAV allows women pastors and leans progressive denominationally; (2) the multi-site streaming model means the congregation watches Stafford's sermon via video rather than hearing Andrew preach, which weakens local pastoral voice and relationship. Worth a visit; go in knowing you're in moderate Baptist territory, not SBC.

churches.assessment: Third Baptist Church of San Francisco is the oldest African-American Baptist congregation west of the Rockies (founded 1852). For nearly half a century — 1976 to 2025 — it was pastored by Rev. Amos C. Brown, a civil-rights leader and close advisor to Kamala Harris. Brown gave the convention prayer at the 2024 DNC. Harris has been a member for more than 20 years and worked for Brown's campaign for San Francisco supervisor in 2000; he was reportedly among the first people she called when Joe Biden suspended his 2024 campaign and she became the presumptive Democratic nominee. Rev. Devon Jerome Crawford succeeded Brown on July 1, 2025. Theologically the congregation operates in the progressive Black social-gospel tradition with heavy reparations and racial-justice framing; ABC-USA affiliation places it on the affirming end of Baptist polity. Per MOOP rubric this is RED; included for situational awareness about the home church of a recent Democratic nominee for President.
churches.denomination_detail: American Baptist Churches USA (ABC-USA) + National Baptist Convention USA dual affiliation; historic Black Baptist congregation founded 1852.
churches.gender_detail: Egalitarian — ABC-USA permits women pastors and elders.

Devon Jerome Crawford as senior pastor since 2025-07-01 (succeeded Rev. Amos C. Brown 1976-2025) + 1399 McAllister St + founded 1852 + Kamala Harris longtime member. churches.overall_label: Promising — Strong Doctrine with Minor Gaps

score_notes.christology: Affirms Jesus as 'the eternal Son of God,' conceived of the Holy Spirit, born of the virgin Mary, 'fully God, fully man.' Substitutionary atonement, bodily resurrection, ascension, and return. Orthodox Christology.
score_notes.scripture: Strong inerrancy affirmation: Bible has 'truth, without any mixture of error, for its matter' and 'all Scripture is totally true and trustworthy.' Scripture is 'the supreme standard by which all human conduct, creeds, and religious opinions should be tried.' Green — clear inerrancy position.
score_notes.gender: GREEN — Complementarian. All-male elder board (7 elders). Lead Teaching Pastor Benjamin Bolin (male). All pastoral/minister titles held by men. Women serve as 'Minister to Preschool and Children' (Pam Reigle) and in director/coordinator roles. Beliefs statement affirms: 'A husband is to love his wife as Christ loved the church. He has the God-given responsibility to provide for, to protect, and to lead his family. A wife is to submit herself graciously to the servant leadership of her husband.' Clear complementarian theology.
score_notes.leadership: Elder-led governance with 7 male elders who 'serve to shepherd and to give oversight' (1 Peter 5:2-3). Lead Teaching Pastor Benjamin Bolin. Senior Associate Pastor Donnie Voss. Multiple ministers for specific areas. Strong accountability structure.
score_notes.soteriology: Comprehensive salvation doctrine: regeneration, justification, sanctification, glorification. 'There is no salvation apart from personal faith in Jesus Christ as Lord.' Sound Reformed Baptist soteriology.
score_notes.cultural: No explicit DEI/CRT language detected. Spanish-language ministry (Travis en Espanol). Community outreach ministries. Historic church. Needs in-person verification but no red flags from website.
score_notes.preaching: Title 'Lead Teaching Pastor' suggests teaching emphasis. Multiple worship styles (choir-led, band-led, Spanish). Unable to verify expository vs. topical from website alone. The strong doctrinal statement suggests substantive preaching.
score_notes.mission: Mission: 'helping people far from God know Christ through global, domestic, and local impact.' Global Mission Coordinator on staff. Community ministries. College ministry. Spanish-language outreach. Great Commission-oriented.
score_notes.mens_discipleship: No dedicated men's ministry found despite having women's ministry programs (CELC & WOW). Small groups and Sunday School exist but no men-specific discipleship. Yellow — gap for a church this size.
score_notes.denominational: Confirmed SBC via SBC.net directory; historic SBC congregation adjacent to SWBTS.

churches.assessment: Travis Avenue Baptist Church is a historic SBC church in Fort Worth led by Lead Teaching Pastor Benjamin Bolin with a 7-member all-male elder board. This is one of the strongest doctrinal profiles in the directory: explicit inerrancy affirmation ('truth, without any mixture of error'), comprehensive salvation theology (regeneration, justification, sanctification, glorification), clear complementarian position in beliefs statement (husband as head, wife submitting graciously), and elder-led governance. The church offers three concurrent worship styles (choir-led, band-led, Spanish) and has strong Great Commission mission language. The main gap is the lack of a dedicated men's ministry despite having women's ministry programs — an oversight for a church with otherwise excellent theological infrastructure. SBC-affiliated with strong denominational accountability. Recommended for evaluation — visit to verify preaching quality and cultural alignment in person.
churches.gender_detail: COMPLEMENTARIAN. All-male elder board (7 elders). All pastoral/minister titles held by men. churches.assessment: President Warren G. Harding joined the Free Baptist Church in Marion on May 6, 1883, served as a trustee for 25 years and as a deacon, and remained a member until his death in 1923. The Free Baptist Church merged with the First Baptist Church via a joint worship service on September 24, 1911, and was renamed Trinity Baptist Church in April 1912. The congregation that today carries Harding's historical pew has, in the contemporary era, embraced a robust 1689 London Baptist Confession Reformed Baptist confessional identity under Pastor Daniel McCoy (DTS / Master's Seminary), with explicit 9Marks and Founders Ministries affiliation. Worth noting: Harding personally was a theologically liberal Baptist (per Patheos historical assessment), so the present-day Trinity Baptist is more confessionally robust than the congregation Harding inhabited.

churches.assessment: Trinity Church Hampton Roads is a multi-campus non-denominational church with a genuinely impressive governance model: a plurality of qualified male elders vetted against 1 Timothy 3 and Titus 1 standards. This is one of the most biblical church governance structures possible. Founded in 2007 from a small prayer group, Trinity now serves multiple communities across Virginia Beach and Norfolk — including campuses near military installations (Princess Anne YMCA, Oceanfront, Downtown Norfolk) and even a campus in Stuttgart, Germany for American military families. The church's stated mission — making disciples who exalt Jesus Christ and honor God's Word — is right on. For Hampton Roads military and veteran men, Trinity Church represents one of the strongest options due to its elder-plurality governance, Scripture-honoring mission, and explicit military community presence. Verify individual campus pastoral leadership and confirm elder gender standards in practice.

churches.assessment: Trinity Presbyterian is Charlottesville's flagship PCA congregation — theologically rigorous, historically grounded, and missionally active. Their tagline 'Seeking the renewal of all things through Jesus Christ' reflects a robust, Christ-centered worldview. As the mother church that planted Grace Community Church, Trinity demonstrates genuine Great Commission commitment. For a Christian man in the Charlottesville area seeking a doctrinally serious, expository-preaching, elder-led church, Trinity Presbyterian belongs at the very top of the list.

churches.assessment: Trinity United Methodist Church is the small-town Kansas Methodist church where Bob Dole grew up — his parents sent the Dole children "most Sundays" per multiple biographies, and the town of Russell held its public memorial farewell to Dole at this church when he died in 2021. The church remains active in the United Methodist Connection — affiliated with the Great Plains Conference. Following the 2019-2023 disaffiliation window, those UMC churches that remained (including Trinity Russell) are now part of a denomination that at General Conference 2024 removed restrictions on ordination of openly gay clergy and same-sex weddings. This places UMC churches at red on MOOP's rubric across gender, cultural, and denominational dimensions — irrespective of any individual rural congregation's personal practice. The local Trinity Russell congregation is small (rural Kansas town of c.4,000), traditional in worship style, and historically significant as Bob Dole's home church.

churches.assessment: Truro Anglican Church is one of the great orthodox Anglican congregations in Northern Virginia. Founded 1843, it has a rich history including connection to national leaders (George Mason was a parishioner of the historic Truro parish). After departing The Episcopal Church over homosexuality and female ordination, Truro joined ACNA and has continued its legacy of faithful biblical Anglicanism. Rector Jamie Brown (since 2022) brings Reformed theological training from RTS combined with Anglican liturgical practice. The Lamb Center (founded 1992 by Truro) demonstrates a long legacy of gospel-motivated community service. Three Sunday services, including an early service — a sign of serious congregational life. For a man wanting orthodox Anglican liturgy, doctrinal clarity, and a congregation with institutional courage, Truro Anglican is excellent.
churches.gender_detail: Male-only ordination (ACNA policy); Truro departed TEC specifically over female ordination — gender clarity is central to their identity

churches.overall_label: Disqualified — Apostate or Anti-Biblical

score_notes.christology: UCC denomination does not require trinitarian affirmation at congregational level; wide theological diversity.
score_notes.scripture: UCC does not affirm inerrancy; Scripture is 'a witness' not final authority in UCC theology.
score_notes.gender: UCC is the most progressive mainline denomination — first to ordain openly gay clergy (1972), first to affirm same-sex marriage (2005). Fully egalitarian.
score_notes.leadership: UCC congregational polity — local governance, but denominational identity is thoroughly progressive.
score_notes.soteriology: UCC theology ranges from universalist to loosely evangelical at the congregational level.
score_notes.cultural: Homepage describes itself as 'a church of extravagant welcome' that 'welcomes and accepts everyone as they are' and aims to 'encourage tolerance, promote social justice' — affirming/progressive UCC posture confirmed on landing page.
score_notes.preaching: Not stated on available sources — verify in person.
score_notes.mission: Stated mission language is 'together, we grow a just and peaceful world' — social-justice framing replaces Great-Commission language; aligns with UCC national identity.
score_notes.denominational: UCC is the most theologically liberal mainline denomination in America.

churches.assessment: The United Church of Christ of Fredericksburg belongs to the most progressive mainline denomination in American Protestantism. The UCC was the first denomination to ordain an openly gay minister (1972) and the first to affirm same-sex marriage (2005). The denomination's 'God is still speaking' campaign and social justice emphasis define its institutional identity. While individual UCC congregations can theoretically be more conservative, the denominational DNA is thoroughly progressive. Rev. Darryl Moch leads. Not recommended for anyone committed to biblical authority and historic orthodoxy.

churches.pastor_credentials: Co-founder and senior pastor; former NFL athlete; Acts 29 executive board member
churches.founded: 2011 (as Renovation Church; rebranded to United Church)
churches.overall_label: Visit with Discernment

score_notes.christology: Acts 29 requires Trinitarian orthodoxy; church emphasizes 'the way of Jesus' and biblical immersion — likely orthodox but creed not named on site.
score_notes.scripture: Acts 29 network requires inerrancy affirmation; church site describes itself as 'Bible based' — inferred green via network, verify on church's own beliefs page.
score_notes.gender: Acts 29 is complementarian (male-only elders/pastors); Crump has publicly affirmed complementarianism — yellow/green.
score_notes.leadership: Elder-led per Acts 29 standards; Crump as dominant teaching voice; leadership page exists.
score_notes.soteriology: Acts 29 affirms Reformed soteriology; Crump has preached sola-fide publicly — likely green via network.
score_notes.cultural: Crump emphasizes race/ethnicity/cultural engagement; has used social-justice adjacent language in past writings (e.g., 'Renovate'); borderline — yellow caution for MOOP audience given rubric's DEI sensitivity.
score_notes.preaching: Crump known for cultural-apologetics/expository blend; 'Purple Church' series on navigating cultural division — mixed expository-topical.
score_notes.mission: Diversity-forward mission ('Revelation 7:9 — every nation, tribe, people'); gospel-proclamation framing.
score_notes.mens_discipleship: Not visible on fetched homepage — verify.
score_notes.denominational: Live homepage emphasizes 'He loves first and then invites us to discover the joy of following Him' — accepting/welcoming framing without explicit doctrinal statement, leadership roster, or Acts 29 affiliation visible on the rendered page. Léonce Crump cultural-engagement track-record still warrants yellow. No wayback snapshot available.

churches.assessment: Renovation Church Atlanta — planted by Leonce Crump Jr. in 2011 with a launch team of 35. Started at King Middle School in Grant Park. NOTE: The church has REBRANDED as 'United Church' with a new location and '75% new' congregation. The 1441 Ponce De Leon Ave address is likely outdated. Kids ministry including Haven Ministry for special needs families. Crump is an author and international speaker. Verify current status — significant transition has occurred. Rebranded from Renovation Church Atlanta; Leonce Crump Jr. remains co-founder and senior pastor; congregation is reportedly ~75% new since the transition.
churches.gender_detail: Verify
churches.denomination_detail: Non-denominational; Acts 29 church-planting network (Léonce Crump serves on Acts 29 executive board)
churches.enrichment_notes: Acts 29 affiliation via Crump's board role provides some accountability. Cultural dimension noted yellow due to Crump's public race-discourse engagement, which MOOP audience may find mixed.

churches.assessment: Vienna Presbyterian Church is a historic PCUSA congregation in Vienna, VA. The PCUSA (Presbyterian Church USA) is the mainline Presbyterian denomination that voted in 2015 to approve same-sex marriage and has long ordained women as elders and pastors. This represents a fundamental departure from the Westminster Confession of Faith, the Reformed theological tradition, and biblical authority on sexuality. Individual PCUSA congregations vary — some maintain more conservative pastoral leadership despite the denomination's drift. However, the denominational framework means that membership contributions flow toward an institution that actively promotes positions contrary to biblical sexuality and clear scriptural authority. For men wanting Reformed theology with denominational integrity, the PCA (Presbyterian Church in America), the OPC (Orthodox Presbyterian Church), or ECO are the sound alternatives. Vienna has multiple PCA and ACNA options that hold the confessional line.

churches.assessment: Vineville Baptist Church (Macon GA) is a moderate-Baptist congregation dual-aligned with the Georgia Baptist Mission Board (SBC) and the Cooperative Baptist Fellowship of Georgia. Senior Pastor Rev. Greg Pope is male, but two of the four pastoral-track positions on the church's staff page are filled by ordained women bearing the title 'Rev.': Rev. Angela Blizzard (Minister of Music, on staff since 2007) and Rev. Leigh Halverson (Minister of Family Life and Education). The church's children's ministry uses CBF curriculum. While the staff use 'Minister' rather than 'Pastor' in formal titling, the practice of ordaining women to staff ministry sits in direct tension with BF&M 2000 Article VI as the SBC currently interprets it.
churches.gender_detail: Minister of Music: Rev. Angela Blizzard (female, ordained, on staff since 2007). Minister of Family Life and Education: Rev. Leigh Halverson (female, ordained). Both carry 'Rev.' honorific indicating ordained pastoral status under moderate-Baptist polity.
churches.denomination_detail: Listed in SBC.net Churches Directory as 'Vineville Baptist Church (Inc).' Also listed on the Cooperative Baptist Fellowship of Georgia churches roster. Dual-aligned SBC (GBMB) / CBF.

churches.assessment: Wallers Baptist Church holds a remarkable distinction: founded in 1769, it claims the title of longest continuously operating Baptist church in the Commonwealth of Virginia — predating the Revolutionary War and the United States itself. That kind of institutional longevity in a rural Spotsylvania County setting speaks to deep community roots and theological stability. The church self-describes with three pillars — 'Bible-believing, Jesus-teaching, and people-loving' — which is clean evangelical language. FaithStreet confirms SBC affiliation, giving a solid denominational foundation on inerrancy, complementarianism, and soteriology. 'Pastor Patrick' is Moop's friend, which is the relational glue that makes this worth visiting. BGAV directory lists a different pastor name (Rev. John Shutlock), which may reflect an outdated directory or a recent pastoral transition to Pastor Patrick. The traditional service format and rural context suggest a conservative, no-frills congregation. No dedicated men's ministry found, but Moop's existing relationship makes this a personal as much as a theological connection.

churches.denomination_detail: Listed in BGAV church directory (bgav.org) AND in FaithStreet as SBC. Rev. John D. Shutlock pastor per BGAV directory. Website itself says only 'Bible-believing, Jesus-teaching, people-loving' with no explicit SBC or BGAV statement and language welcoming 'people of all ages, races, and backgrounds'. BGAV dual-alignment is a moderate yellow signal in VA context.

churches.assessment: Washington Community Fellowship is a long-standing evangelical congregation in NE Washington, DC (Capitol Hill area) with Mennonite/Anabaptist roots, describing itself as 'Christ-centered' and called to personal transformation, authentic community, and social impact. The Anabaptist tradition (Mennonite, Brethren) is one of the historic Reformation streams, historically emphasizing discipleship, community, peacemaking, and radical following of Jesus. Strengths: genuine community emphasis, NE DC neighborhood engagement, ecumenical but Christ-centered orientation. Cautions: Anabaptist traditions vary widely on Scripture's authority and gender roles; many Mennonite-affiliated churches have moved toward egalitarian and progressive positions. Review their current statement of faith, pastoral authority structure, and specific positions on gender and sexuality. A community-focused church with historic roots — warrants direct investigation.

churches.assessment: Washington National Cathedral is an architectural masterpiece and a significant national landmark — but from a USMC Ministries theological alignment standpoint, it is firmly not recommended. The Episcopal Church (TEC) has abandoned biblical authority on human sexuality, ordains women as bishops and priests, performs same-sex marriages, and its leadership uses the pulpit for progressive political advocacy. Bishop Mariann Budde's nationally publicized January 2025 inaugural sermon was a political statement, not a Gospel proclamation. The Cathedral has hosted interfaith services including Islamic prayers. The beauty of the building and the grandeur of the liturgy should not be confused with theological fidelity. This is included in the directory for situational awareness — military and government personnel in DC will be invited to events here. Know what you're walking into.

churches.assessment: West End Presbyterian is a PCA congregation in Richmond's West End — and PCA means a lot here. The Presbyterian Church in America is one of the most theologically rigorous denominations in America: inerrancy of Scripture, Westminster Confession of Faith, male-only elders, faith-alone soteriology, and complementarian theology are all baked into the PCA constitution. Rev. Steven Shelby leads a church with a clearly stated mission: 'make followers of Jesus who bring the Gospel to bear on every facet of life and culture.' The staff includes associate pastors for youth and neighborhood outreach, suggesting a full-orbed ministry. For any man seeking a doctrinally robust, Gospel-centered, Word-saturated church home in Richmond, West End Presbyterian belongs at the top of the list.

churches.assessment: Sen. John H. Glenn Jr. (D-OH), Marine fighter pilot, first American to orbit Earth (Friendship 7, 1962), four-term U.S. Senator (1974-1999), and at age 77 the oldest astronaut in spaceflight (STS-95, 1998), was raised in this New Concord congregation by his parents John Herschel and Clara Glenn. Glenn's mother was the first female Ruling Elder ordained at Westminster; his father was also a Ruling Elder. Glenn himself was a lifelong Presbyterian Ruling Elder. He and his wife Annie alternated between Westminster (John's family) and College Drive Presbyterian (Annie's family) during their hometown visits. In Washington he attended National Presbyterian Church and served on its Session. The church is currently a PC(USA) mainline congregation under Rev. Ellen Thomas, reflecting denominational shifts that occurred decades after Glenn's formation.

churches.assessment: Winona Lake Grace Church sits in the Indiana college-and-seminary town that serves as the geographic hub of the Charis Fellowship — Grace College, Grace Theological Seminary, and the national Charis office are all in Winona Lake. Lead Pastor Kip Cone is Grace College and Grace Seminary trained, served almost a decade as a missionary in Berlin, Germany with Encompass World Partners (formerly Grace Brethren International Missions), and has been on the church's pastoral staff since 2006. The Charis Fellowship is dispensational evangelical-Anabaptist, complementarian, biblically-inerrantist. For a northern-Indiana man wanting a Bible-rooted, mission-minded Grace Brethren church in the heart of the denomination's institutional life, Winona Lake Grace deserves a careful look.

churches.assessment: The Woodlands Methodist Church is the single largest church in the Global Methodist Church — 14,000 members who voted 96% to depart the UMC and join the GMC in 2023. That kind of institutional courage (leaving a denomination with all the attendant property and legal costs) signals a congregation serious about orthodox Wesleyan teaching. Rev. Mark Sorensen took over as Senior Pastor from the long-tenured Rev. Dr. Ed Robb in 2021, holds an M.Div from Asbury Theological Seminary, and has served the church since 2013. The church operates two campuses in the Houston suburbs, runs a preschool and a private elementary school, and offers 10 live and online worship services weekly. As with all GMC churches, the local stance on women as elders should be verified (the Texas conference varies), but the overall profile is solidly orthodox, Trinitarian, traditional-marriage Wesleyan.

churches.assessment: Zion BIC in Abilene is one of the founding Brethren in Christ congregations west of the Mississippi, organized in 1887 by River Brethren immigrants from Pennsylvania. The congregation has a notable missions-sending history within the BIC denomination, having produced numerous missionaries and church leaders. Pastor Jay Johnson currently leads, with Thomas Price as youth pastor. The 130-year heritage, plain Anabaptist roots, and small-town Kansas setting make this a meaningful spiritual home for those drawn to peace-church traditions. Yellow rating reflects the BIC denomination's allowance of female pastors, which the local Zion staff does not currently practice.

churches.assessment: Zion Presbyterian Church is one of the most theologically rigorous options in the Fredericksburg area. It is a congregation of the Free Church of Scotland (Continuing) — a denomination that holds to Biblical inerrancy and the original Westminster Confession of Faith without modification. This is not the touchy-feely mainline PCUSA Presbyterian; this is hard-core Westminster Calvinist confessionalism. Pastor Rom Prakashpalan is a converted Hindu/atheist who came to faith through hearing the Gospel (Romans 10:17), graduated RPTS with an MDiv, and was installed here in November 2024. The church is very new (2023) and meets at Fredericksburg Christian School. Two Sunday services (10:30 AM and 2:00 PM) plus a Thursday prayer meeting demonstrate seriousness. The lack of men's ministry is understandable for a plant this young. For a man who wants unapologetic Reformed confessionalism and a pastor with a powerful conversion testimony, this is a must-visit.

churches.assessment: Truth Bible Church is an independent Baptist Bible church in Hollywood, Maryland (Southern Maryland), planted in 2008 and now led by Dr. Joshua West, who holds a Th.M and a Th.D in systematic theology from Trinity College of the Bible and Theological Seminary. Its statement of faith affirms the inerrancy of Scripture, the Trinity, orthodox Christology (virgin birth, physical resurrection, substitutionary atonement), and salvation by grace alone through faith alone, with believer's baptism by immersion. The church is governed by a plurality of male elders (Dr. Joshua West, Dr. Alden Laird, Dr. Dennis Richardson, and Dan Ensminger), with no women in pastoral or elder roles and distinct Men of Truth and Women of Truth ministries, which places it clearly in complementarian practice; discipleship runs through Home Groups and one-to-one counseling, and missions are pursued both locally and through Pastor West's work with the church-planting ministry Compel International. The clearest signal comes from West's own published theology: Hard Sayings: Reconciling the Cost of Discipleship and the American Dream and Come and Die press a costly, counter-consumerist discipleship and openly reject the feel-good preaching that never calls sinners to repentance, while The Power of Preaching and his verse-by-verse Romans volumes point to expository, doctrinally serious preaching. The church website (Wix) is sparse and was mid-transition, but the leadership page, an active Facebook (TBCMaryland) and Instagram presence, and the pastor's substantial public writing together substantiate a green rating rather than a default yellow.
churches.denomination_detail: Independent Baptist polity — elder/deacon governance; no stated denominational affiliation

Richardson, Ensminger), Pastor West's personal site joshuawest.net plus his published books (Hard Sayings, Come and Die, The Power of Preaching, Romans vols), and the church's active Facebook (TBCMaryland) and Instagram. Credentials confirmed: Th.M + Th.D systematic theology (Trinity College of the Bible & Theological Seminary). Evidence base per category: complementarian (all-male eldership), expository preaching, costly/counter-consumerist discipleship, missions via Compel International.

churches.overall_label: GREEN — Confessional CREC congregation; plural male eldership, covenant-renewal worship, classical Christian education, and a robustly counter-secular Reformed posture under Pastor Duane Garner.

score_notes.christology: Green — Trinitarian and orthodox; the church’s whole life is ordered around “the community of the Trinity… realized in the community of the Church,” and it confesses no hope for sinners “apart from the saving mercy and the work of the Lord Jesus Christ.”
score_notes.scripture: Green — Holds the Bible as “absolutely authoritative… the ultimate authority of our thinking,” and subscribes to the historic Reformed confessions and catechisms (Westminster standards within the CREC).
score_notes.mens_discipleship: Green — Strong covenant-household and classical-education ethos typical of CREC congregations; a large board of male deacons and an emphasis on raising and discipling households.
score_notes.soteriology: Green — Reformed and monergistic: “All men are sinners, justly deserving God’s wrath and without hope apart from… the Lord Jesus Christ.” Salvation by grace through faith within the covenant.
score_notes.gender: Green — Patriarchal/complementarian by conviction; governed by a plurality of male elders (Session) and male deacons only, with no women in office; family-integrated, covenant-renewal worship.
score_notes.leadership: Green — Elder-led Session (Pastor Duane Garner, Associate Pastor Peter Jones, plus ruling elders John Mitchell, Scott Moonen, Nathaniel Talbott) with a full board of deacons — plural male eldership.
score_notes.preaching: Green — Reformed, text-driven preaching set within covenant-renewal (liturgical) worship, with heavy Scripture reading and Psalm-singing.
score_notes.mission: Green — Great Commission pursued through covenant faithfulness, household discipleship, and Christian education, with an optimistic (postmillennial) eschatology.
score_notes.cultural: Green — Explicitly counter-secular and confessional; a “mere Christendom” / biblical-theocracy posture that is the opposite of DEI/CRT or social-justice drift.
score_notes.denominational: Green — Member of the CREC (Communion of Reformed Evangelical Churches); Pastor Duane Garner serves as Presiding Minister of the CREC’s Augustine Presbytery — strong external accountability plus elder plurality.

churches.denomination_detail: CREC — Augustine Presbytery. Confessional, covenantal, paedobaptist Reformed; covenant-renewal (liturgical) worship, Psalm-singing, classical Christian education.
churches.pastor_credentials: Bachelor of Bible Languages, Oxford Baptist Institute (Oxford, MS); four years at the Bucer Institute for Biblical Studies; ACBC-certified biblical counselor; Presiding Minister of the CREC’s Augustine Presbytery. churches.assessment: Christ Church is a CREC (Communion of Reformed Evangelical Churches) congregation meeting in Morrisville, North Carolina, led by Pastor Duane Garner — an ACBC-certified biblical counselor who also serves as Presiding Minister of the CREC’s Augustine Presbytery. It is confessional and covenantal: the Bible is “absolutely authoritative,” the historic Reformed confessions and catechisms are its doctrinal summary, worship follows the covenant-renewal pattern with Psalm-singing, and the congregation is governed by a plurality of male elders and deacons. Its culture is family-integrated, classically educated, and robustly counter-secular. An acquaintance of MOOP recommended it as “super solid” — free of the wokeness, CRT, and female-leadership concerns this directory screens for. It earns green across all ten categories.

churches.assessment: Grace Presbyterian Church is a confessional Presbyterian Church in America (PCA) congregation in Aiken, South Carolina, holding the Westminster Confession and Catechisms as “our only rule for faith and life.” It keeps the traditional Reformed rhythm — morning and evening worship, Wednesday men’s and women’s Bible studies, and a monthly Lord’s Supper — and is led by a plurality of male elders under Palmetto Presbytery. An acquaintance of MOOP whose family attends describes the pastor as excellent and the culture as explicitly patriarchal and family-integrated, with head coverings common among the women and a large contingent of young families; the fellowship meals are a highlight and the main critique is simply a lengthy service. It earns green across all ten categories. (Identification note: an acquaintance of MOOP recommended “Grace Presbyterian (PCA)” without a city; this Aiken congregation is the strong match by denomination and proximity to the Springfield, SC daughter-church plant they described — confirm if a direct link is available.)

churches.assessment: Citylight Church Dover is a new Citylight plant in Dover, York County, Pennsylvania. It began gathering in 2026 and meets Sundays at 4:00 PM at 6390 Harmony Grove Road, Dover, PA 17315. Their site names Andy Resh as the lead planter: MTS and STM from Grimke Seminary, planter and former lead pastor of Citylight Delco. Alex Kocman, an elder at Faith Bible Fellowship Church of York and a staff member at ABWE, has publicly said he and his family are preparing to transition here over the coming months. He will help lead worship and enter a season of pastoral development. He is staying at ABWE. He is not the lead pastor of this church. The move is on good terms with the elders at Faith, not a conflict. Public distinctives include gospel centrality, God's sovereignty in saving sinners, continuationist spiritual gifts, complementarian leadership, and believer's baptism. This listing is from those public pages and from Kocman's public update. Sermons have not been reviewed, so this is Visit with Discernment, not a full green. To support their ministry, their site says give at https://citylightdover.com/give/ and select Citylight York. Faith Bible Fellowship page: https://usmcmin.org/churches/faith-bible-fellowship-york-pa.html
